title: How to find compromised passwords on iPhone and Android
summary: Apple and Google password managers can flag compromised, weak and reused passwords on your phone before credential stuffing attacks can strike.
story: Google General Counsel Halimah Delaine Prado joins 'Fox & Friends' to detail how Google is fighting AI-powered phishing scams.

You probably have more passwords than you realize. Banking, email, shopping accounts and streaming services can add up quickly. The bigger problem comes when one of those passwords lands in a data leak and you have no idea it happened. Your phone may already know about it.

Both Apple and Google can check saved passwords for security problems and warn you when a login appears compromised. Apple can also flag passwords that are weak or reused. Google Password Manager offers a Password Checkup that can identify compromised, reused or weak passwords. That gives you a chance to fix an exposed login before someone tries to use it against you.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways AI can help you get better healthcare.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class Get Better Healthcare With AI has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
FAKE PASSWORD-MANAGER ALERTS COULD PUT YOUR VAULT AT RISK
An iPhone can warn you when a saved password appears in a known data leak and prompt you to change it. (David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Your phone may already know which passwords need attention

Password alerts are one of those security features that can quietly sit on your phone until you actually open them. When you do, you might be surprised by what you find. On iPhone, Apple says the Passwords app automatically identifies common weaknesses, including passwords that are easy to guess or used multiple times. Your iPhone can also securely monitor saved passwords and warn you when they appear in known data leaks. Google Password Manager offers a similar check for credentials stored in your Google Account. Google says it can identify passwords that were exposed, are weak or are being used across multiple accounts. Checking only takes a minute.
How to find compromised passwords on iPhone
On an iPhone running iOS 27:

Open the Passwords app.Authenticate with Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode if prompted.Tap Security.Review any accounts that Apple has flagged.Tap an account to see why Apple recommends changing the password.Tap Change Password and update the password on the website or in the app.
Open the Passwords app.
Authenticate with Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode if prompted.
Tap Security.
Review any accounts that Apple has flagged.
Tap an account to see why Apple recommends changing the password.
Tap Change Password and update the password on the website or in the app.

Apple may flag a login because the password appeared in a known data leak. You can also see recommendations for passwords that are weak or reused. If the website supports it, you may also be able to switch to a passkey or upgrade to Sign in with Apple. Otherwise, your iPhone can help create a strong replacement password for many accounts.
Make sure compromised password detection is turned on
While you are checking your passwords, make sure the monitoring feature itself is enabled.
On iOS 27:
Open Settings.Tap Apps.Tap Passwords.Make sure Detect Compromised Passwords is turned on.
Open Settings.
Tap Apps.
Tap Passwords.
Make sure Detect Compromised Passwords is turned on.

Apple confirms that this setting allows the iPhone to monitor saved passwords and warn you when they appear in known data leaks. It is an easy setting to overlook, and I would rather have my phone warn me than discover an exposed password after someone has already tried to use it.
GOOGLE DOCS PASSWORD LEAK REVEALS A COSTLY SECURITY MISTAKE
Google Password Manager’s Password Checkup can flag compromised, reused and weak passwords saved to your Google Account. (Thomas Trutschel/Photothek via Getty Images)
How to find compromised passwords on Samsung Galaxy

These steps are based on the latest Samsung One UI 9 software, which is built on Android 17. Samsung began its broader One UI 9 rollout in September 2026, although availability varies by phone model, carrier and region. Galaxy phones can save login information with Google Password Manager, Samsung Pass or another password manager. If your passwords are saved with Google, the most reliable way to check them for security problems is through Chrome.
To check passwords saved with Google Password Manager:
Open Chrome.Tap the three-dot menu.Tap Settings.Tap Google Password Manager.Tap Checkup.Review any passwords flagged as compromised, reused or weak.
Open Chrome.
Tap the three-dot menu.
Tap Settings.
Tap Google Password Manager.
Tap Checkup.
Review any passwords flagged as compromised, reused or weak.
Google Password Manager can identify passwords that were exposed in a data breach. It can also flag passwords that are weak or used for more than one account.

If you use Samsung Pass instead, keep in mind that Samsung documents it as a service for storing and autofilling login information using biometric authentication. Samsung Pass is also integrated with Samsung Wallet on supported Galaxy devices. Samsung does not currently document the same compromised-password checking feature that Google provides through Password Checkup.

To review login information stored with Samsung Pass, open Samsung Wallet and access Samsung Pass. If you want active breach monitoring and password-health tools, a dedicated password manager can provide additional protection.
How to find compromised passwords on Google Pixel

These steps are based on Android 17 with the latest September 2026 Pixel software. Google began rolling out its September 2026 Pixel update to supported Android 17 devices on September 15, with availability varying by carrier and device. On current Pixel phones, look for the Passwords app. Google says this app provides a shortcut to Google Password Manager, where you can access passwords and passkeys saved to your Google Account.
To check for compromised passwords, the most consistently documented route is through Chrome:

Open Chrome.Tap the three-dot menu.Tap Settings.Tap Google Password Manager.Tap Checkup.Review any passwords flagged as compromised, reused or weak.Select a flagged account and follow the prompts to change the password.
Open Chrome.
Tap the three-dot menu.
Tap Settings.
Tap Google Password Manager.
Tap Checkup.
Review any passwords flagged as compromised, reused or weak.
Select a flagged account and follow the prompts to change the password.

You can also open the Passwords app to quickly access Google Password Manager. If you do not see the app, open Settings, search for Password Manager and select it. Google Password Manager can warn you when saved credentials have been exposed online. It can also identify weak passwords and passwords being used for more than one account.
IDENTITY RESTORATION: WHAT TO DO AFTER IDENTITY THEFT
Turning on the detect compromised passwords setting lets your iPhone monitor saved logins and alert you when one may have been exposed. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)
What does a compromised password warning actually mean?

Seeing the word compromised can make your stomach drop. However, the warning does not automatically mean someone has already logged into your account. Apple can alert you when a password appears in a known data leak. Google can warn you when one of your saved passwords has been published online or otherwise identified as compromised.

Either way, I would take the warning seriously. An exposed password may already be available to criminals even if nobody has successfully used it against your account yet. One risk is credential stuffing. Criminals take usernames and passwords obtained from previous breaches and try the same combinations on other services. That is why reusing a password can turn one exposed login into a much bigger headache.
What to do when your phone flags a password

Start by going directly to the company's official website or app and changing the password there. Avoid using a password-reset link from an unexpected email or text. Criminals know breach warnings get your attention, and phishing messages can use that fear against you.

Next, check whether you used the same password somewhere else. If you did, change it on those accounts too. Each important account should have its own strong password so one exposed login cannot easily be reused somewhere else.

Then, add two-factor authentication (2FA) when the account supports it. We recommend turning on 2-Step Verification for stronger protection of your saved sign-in information. You should also consider passkeys when they are available. Passkeys can replace traditional passwords on supported accounts and are designed to provide stronger protection against phishing.
When a dedicated password manager may make more sense

Apple Passwords and Google Password Manager are convenient, especially if most of your devices live inside one ecosystem. However, plenty of us bounce between an iPhone, a Windows PC, a Mac or different browsers during the day. That is where a dedicated password manager can become especially useful.

A dedicated password manager can keep one encrypted vault synced across multiple devices and platforms. Many also work with major browsers, so your logins can follow you when you switch between computers, phones and tablets. Features such as autofill and password generation can also make it easier to use a different strong password for every account.

Some password managers add security tools that can flag weak or reused passwords and alert you when saved credentials may have appeared in a breach. For someone with dozens or even hundreds of logins, that gives you one central place to generate passwords, store them and keep an eye on their security.
Check out the best expert-reviewed password managers of 2026 at Cyberguy.com.
Pay extra attention to your most important accounts

If your password check produces a long list of warnings, you do not need to panic and change everything at once. I would start with your primary email account. Password-reset links for many of your other accounts probably land there, making email an especially valuable target. Then deal with financial accounts, your Apple or Google account and services holding sensitive personal information. After that, work through the rest of the warnings. If you find an account you abandoned years ago and no longer need, consider closing it instead of leaving another forgotten login sitting online.
Reused passwords can turn one breach into a much bigger problem

Suppose a small website you joined years ago suffers a breach. You may barely remember creating the account. If that old password matches one you still use somewhere important, criminals now have a combination they can try somewhere else. Using the same password on multiple accounts raises your risk if one of those passwords gets stolen. This is one reason a password manager can help. You do not have to come up with a memorable variation every time you create an account. The manager can generate a unique password and remember it for you.
Do not ignore the alerts after you clean everything up

Running a password check once is helpful, but leave the monitoring features enabled afterward. Apple can continue watching saved passwords for appearances in known leaks. Google Password Manager also continues checking passwords and can notify you when saved credentials are found online. Google even allows you to control its password alerts from Password Manager settings. That turns your password manager into an early-warning system rather than something you only open after a breach makes the news.
Kurt's key takeaways

What I like about these password checks is that they do some of the detective work for you. You do not have to remember every company that suffered a breach or wonder whether an old password is still floating around online. Your phone or password manager can flag trouble and give you a chance to deal with it. I would start by checking the passwords already saved on your phone. Fix anything marked compromised, pay close attention to reused passwords and leave the alerts turned on afterward. If you move between several devices or want more security tools in one place, a dedicated password manager can also make the whole process easier to manage.
When was the last time you checked your saved passwords for security warnings, and how many compromised or reused passwords do you think you would find? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

title: Texas executes Jamaal Howard despite concerns over lethal injection drug used in failed Tennessee execution
summary: Jamaal Howard's attorneys cited Christa Pike's failed lethal injection in Tennessee to argue the pentobarbital drug posed risks, but the Supreme Court rejected it.
story: Christa Pike asked "Where am I?" and "Who are you?" after unexpectedly waking up Tuesday following a botched lethal injection last week, according to her attorney Randy Spivey. He said her team had believed she was "brain dead" before she awoke.

A Texas man convicted of killing a convenience store clerk during a robbery was executed Wednesday evening after the Supreme Court declined to halt the execution, despite his attorneys raising concerns about the lethal injection drug used in a failed execution attempt in Tennessee last week.
Jamaal Howard, 46, was pronounced dead at 8:03 p.m. He was sentenced to death for the 2000 killing of 42-year-old Vickie Swartout in Silsbee, Texas.

Prior to Howard's execution, his attorneys pointed to the failed execution of Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike, who survived two doses of pentobarbital on Sept. 30, arguing that the same drug Texas planned to use could pose similar risks.
"Texas should not be eager to follow in Tennessee’s footsteps; a stay would keep that from happening," Howard's attorneys argued in their filing.
CHRISTA PIKE'S ATTORNEYS SAY SHE'S IN CRITICAL CONDITION AFTER BOTCHED LETHAL INJECTIONS

The U.S. Supreme Court declined to halt Jamaal Howard's execution after his attorneys raised concerns about the lethal injection drug used by Texas. (Texas Department of Criminal Justice; AP Photo/Pat Sullivan)
The Supreme Court rejected Howard's emergency appeal without explanation. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson was the only justice to publicly dissent, Fox News reported.
The Texas Court of Criminal Appeals had previously rejected two requests to stop the execution based on concerns about the drug's use.
According to The Associated Press, as the pentobarbital began taking effect Wednesday evening, Howard took a couple of breaths and gasped.

Howard then began making snoring sounds, coughed and resumed the snoring sounds, which grew progressively quieter. His movements reportedly stopped entirely after around 30 seconds, and he was pronounced dead 19 minutes later.
CHRISTA PIKE’S BOTCHED LETHAL INJECTION TAKES FOCUS OFF VICTIM, JEOPARDIZES EXECUTION: FORMER POLICE CHIEF
Jamaal Howard, 46, was executed in Texas on Oct. 7, 2026, for the 2000 killing of convenience store clerk Vickie Swartout. (Texas Department of Criminal Justice)
Howard's attorneys also said in court filings that they had requested information about the dose of pentobarbital the Texas Department of Criminal Justice planned to use to carry out the execution.
The concerns stemmed in part from Pike's execution attempt, during which she reportedly survived two doses of pentobarbital.

Howard's execution took place the same day a Tennessee judge granted a request from Pike's attorneys to order the Tennessee Department of Correction to preserve evidence connected to the failed execution attempt.
According to the Death Penalty Information Center, Pike is the first person to survive a lethal injection in the modern era.
CHRISTA PIKE EXECUTION FAILURE SPARES MURDERER WHO BAILED VICTIM OUT JUST TO KILL HIM

Randy Spivey, an attorney for Christa Pike, a death row prisoner who survived a botched execution, speaks to the media, flanked by Luke Ihnen, after a Tennessee court was presented a status update on Pike, outside a courtroom in Nashville, Tennessee, Oct. 7, 2026. (Reuters/Seth Herald)

Howard's attorneys also argued before the Supreme Court that his execution should be halted because he was intellectually disabled. However, the state said his attorneys had not presented evidence establishing that he met the legal criteria for intellectual disability.

Howard, who was 20 years old at the time, also took $114 from the cash register during the robbery.

title: FIRST ON FOX: US Coast Guard recruits largest class in nearly 40 years, beats goals for third straight year
summary: The Coast Guard enlisted 5,445 active-duty members in fiscal year 2026, its largest class in nearly four decades as Force Design aims to add 15,000.
story: Fox News correspondent Brooke Taylor reports on U.S. military recruitment achievements under the Trump administration on ‘Special Report.’

FIRST ON FOX: The U.S. Coast Guard recruited its largest enlisted class in nearly four decades during fiscal year 2026, surpassing its recruiting goals for the third consecutive year as the service works to expand its ranks.
According to the Coast Guard, 5,445 active-duty members enlisted in fiscal year 2026, up from 5,204 in 2025 and 4,422 in 2024.
The service also commissioned 346 active-duty officers, the second-highest total in its history.
"These record-breaking recruitment numbers prove that the call to serve still resonates deeply across our country," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a statement.
US ARMY HITS 2026 RECRUITING GOALS FOUR MONTHS EARLY, PETE HEGSETH ANNOUNCES AT WEST POINT COMMENCEMENT
The U.S. Coast Guard enlisted 5,445 active-duty recruits in fiscal year 2026, marking its largest recruiting class in nearly four decades. (U.S. Coast Guard)

"I am incredibly proud to stand beside these new Coast Guard men and women who have stepped up to defend our homeland," he continued. "They represent the very best of who we are, and we are going to make sure they have the tools, the training and the support to get the job done."
During fiscal year 2026, the Coast Guard expanded its recruiting efforts, opening four recruiting offices in Miami, Florida; Long Island, New York; Austin, Texas; and the Netherlands.
Coast Guard Vice Commandant Adm. Tom Allan said the numbers reflect growing interest in serving.
COAST GUARD ENDING RACE-BASED ADMISSIONS FOR OFFICER COMMISSIONING PROGRAM UNDER TRUMP DEI CRACKDOWN
The U.S. Coast Guard surpassed its recruiting goals for the third consecutive year in fiscal year 2026. (U.S. Coast Guard)
"We surpassed our recruiting goals because Americans are ready and willing to serve in the U.S. Coast Guard, conducting exciting missions that deliver results our Nation needs," Allan said.

"This momentum is about more than numbers; it is about being the world’s best Coast Guard and building the workforce America needs," he added. "We are proud to welcome our newest members and grateful to our recruiters for continuing to deliver exceptional results."
The service is also investing in new infrastructure to help train its expanding workforce.
The Coast Guard awarded a $400 million contract to modernize Training Center Cape May in New Jersey, marking the largest shore construction award in the service's history.
TRUMP TURNS TO EMERGING TECH GIANT IN MULTI-BILLION BID TO RAMP UP US SUBMARINE PRODUCTION
The U.S. Coast Guard reported 5,445 active-duty enlistments and 346 newly commissioned active-duty officers during fiscal year 2026. (U.S. Coast Guard)
The facility serves as the Coast Guard's sole basic training center for enlisted recruits, and the improvements are intended to accommodate its growing workforce.
The recruitment gains come as the Coast Guard pursues a modernization initiative known as Force Design.

title: Driver opens fire on strangers along major US interstate, tells cops he ‘had to kill people today’
summary: Andrew Darrick Tanaka allegedly told police, "I had to kill people today," after allegedly opening fire on vehicles along Interstate 35 in Warren County.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
An Iowa man accused of opening fire on passing vehicles along an interstate and wounding a woman allegedly made a chilling admission to police after his arrest, according to court documents.

Andrew Darrick Tanaka, 27, of West Des Moines, faces four counts of attempted murder in Monday afternoon's shootings along Interstate 35 in Warren County, according to the Iowa Department of Public Safety.
After being taken into custody, Tanaka allegedly told law enforcement, "I had to kill people today," according to a criminal complaint and affidavit filed Tuesday in Warren County District Court.

The incident began around 3:31 p.m. Monday when authorities received multiple 911 calls reporting gunfire along the northbound lanes of I-35.VIDEO SHOWS IOWA ROAD RAGE SUSPECT SURRENDER AFTER POLICE ORDER HIM TO DROP GUN
Andrew Darrick Tanaka, 27, faces four counts of attempted murder after allegedly opening fire on multiple vehicles along Interstate 35 in Iowa Oct. 5, 2026. (Iowa Department of Public Safety)
Tanaka was driving a black Chevrolet Equinox when a woman driving a black BMW passed him on the interstate, according to the affidavit. The BMW then passed a Subaru Outback.
Investigators allege Tanaka caught up to the Subaru and fired at least two rounds through the driver's side window, striking the woman behind the wheel in her left shoulder.
He then allegedly caught up to the BMW and fired another round through its driver's side window.

Tanaka continued north before rear-ending a gray Nissan Altima carrying two people, according to the affidavit.APPARENT ROAD RAGE DRIVER APPEARS TO THREATEN MOM ON CAMERA AS 3-YEAR-OLD CRIES IN BACK SEAT

title: Mom dies shielding baby in horrific 15-story Bronx fall as police hunt suspect: report
summary: Angel Carrasco is wanted after Nathaly Ramirez, 23, was allegedly pushed from a 15th-floor Bronx balcony with her baby in a suspected domestic violence attack.
story: New York City Police Department detectives are searching for Angel Carrasco after Nathaly Ramirez and her 8-month-old daughter pushed from a Bronx apartment balcony, police say. (Credit: FOX 5 New York)

A New York City mother and her baby were allegedly pushed from an apartment balcony in a deadly attack that left the woman dead and her infant daughter critically injured, police said, as detectives hunt a man wanted in connection with the case.
The NYPD identified Angel Carrasco, 31, as the man detectives are seeking after Nathaly Ramirez, 23, and her 8-month-old daughter were found outside their Bronx apartment building early Tuesday.

The pair fell from a 15th-floor balcony, according to FOX 5 NY, which reported that investigators were looking for Ramirez’s boyfriend or recent ex-boyfriend in a suspected domestic violence incident.
GEORGIA COLLEGE STUDENT MIRACULOUSLY SURVIVES 8-STORY PLUNGE AFTER METAL BENCH BREAKS HER FALL

Investigators believe Ramirez tightly embraced her daughter during the fall, likely cushioning the baby from the impact, ABC7 NY reported.
Neighbors described hearing a desperate plea moments before the horrifying incident.
"Please don’t do this!" Ramirez screamed, according to neighbors cited by FOX 5.

Officers responded to a 911 call at approximately 3:38 a.m. Tuesday outside 2550 Olinville Ave., where they found Ramirez and her daughter with injuries indicating a fall from an elevated position, the NYPD told Fox News Digital.
DATING-APP CHARMER ACCUSED OF MURDER AFTER HISTORY OF DOMESTIC ARRESTS INVOLVING WOMEN HE MET ONLINE
Nathaly Ramirez and her 8-month-old daughter were found outside this apartment building in the Bronx early Tuesday. Police determined both had been pushed from a balcony. (FOX 5 New York)
"Further investigation determined that both individuals had been pushed from a balcony," the department said.
Officers rushed the baby to a hospital in critical condition. Emergency medical personnel transported Ramirez to a hospital, where she was later pronounced dead.

Police identified Carrasco as wanted in connection with the incident in an update Wednesday and released an image of him. The department’s statement did not specify his relationship to Ramirez or announce any charges.

Sources told FOX 5 that the couple had a history of domestic violence and that police had been called to the apartment multiple times. A woman who lives two doors down told the outlet she had heard yelling from the apartment on numerous occasions.
MARYLAND DAD BLAMED 'SATAN' AFTER 2-MONTH-OLD DAUGHTER DIED FROM HORRIFIC HEAD TRAUMA
Angel Carrasco, 31, is wanted in connection with the incident that killed Nathaly Ramirez and critically injured her infant daughter, the NYPD said. (NYPD Crime Stoppers)

"He was kicking the door down trying to get into the apartment," Mike told the station.

Christa Pike's lawyers believed the Tennessee death row inmate was "brain dead" and expected her to be taken off life support before she unexpectedly woke up Tuesday, nearly a week after the state failed two attempts to lethally inject her.

"To the shock of everyone, including me, including her team and including the medical team, Christa woke up and began talking," Randy Spivey, one of her attorneys, told reporters Wednesday after a court hearing in Nashville.

"We believe in the sanctity of human life."
The parents of murdered Texas mother Christa Bauer Gilley, 38, have made their first public statements following their daughter's killing.

Lee Mongerson Gilley is accused of murdering his wife, Christa Bauer Gilley, and their unborn child in Houston in 2024. (Christa Bauer Gilley/Facebook; Melissa Phillip/Houston Chronicle via Getty Images)
LEE GILLEY BEGS FOR ITALIAN PROTECTION AS ALLEGED SQUATTER TARGETS HOME WHERE PREGNANT WIFE WAS KILLED

title: California couple charged with abusing 14 surrogate-born children inside $10M Los Angeles mansion
summary: Security footage from the couple's $10 million Arcadia mansion allegedly revealed systematic beatings of 14 surrogate-born children by nannies and parents.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A California couple faces severe felony charges after allegedly abusing at least 14 surrogate-born children — some as young as 2 months old — inside their multimillion-dollar Arcadia mansion, according to authorities.

Guojun Xuan, 66, and Silvia Zhang, 39, were each charged with one count of conspiracy to commit child abuse. Xuan also faces one felony count of child abuse, one felony count of accessory after the fact and five felony counts of dissuading a witness. Zhang faces an additional count of accessory after the fact and four counts of dissuading a witness. Both have pleaded not guilty.
MICHIGAN NURSE ACCUSED OF BREAKING BONES AND BRUISING PREMATURE INFANT AT CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL
"The number of children who were subjected to this alleged horrific abuse is unprecedented," Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman said.
"The alleged corporal abuse of these children is appalling and revolting, especially at the hands of those who were supposed to protect them."

Guojun Xuan and Silvia Zhang appeared for their arraignment in Pasadena, Calif., Tuesday, on charges of abuse of at least 14 surrogate-born children, some as young as 2 months old, at an Arcadia mansion where they lived. (Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)

An investigation was launched in May 2025 when Zhang brought her 2-month-old infant to Children's Hospital Los Angeles with a traumatic head injury and severe brain bleeding, affiliate FOX 11 Los Angeles reported. Medical staff determined the infant had been violently shaken and struck by a nanny, Chunmei Li, according to the report.

Prosecutors allege that Zhang and Xuan delayed seeking medical attention for two days, bringing the child to the hospital only after he began experiencing seizures. The couple allegedly made false claims that the baby had fallen out of bed.
OHIO MOM OF 16 CRADLES STOMACH IN COURT, PLEADS NOT GUILTY IN SEVERE ABUSE CASE INVOLVING OWN CHILDREN

Security footage recovered by police from the couple's $10 million home revealed widespread, systemic abuse against 14 surrogate-born children ranging in age from 2 months to 13 years old, with the majority between ages 1 and 3.
Six additional children linked to the couple were later located at other homes, bringing the total number of affected children to 21.
The Arcadia, California home where Guojun Xuan, 66, and Silvia Zhang, 39, allegedly abused multiple surrogate-born children.  (Jesse Watson / Fox News Digital)

Inside the mansion, prosecutors discovered three "learning centers" where toddlers were forced to sit at desks for hours. Nannies inside the home were allegedly instructed to administer discipline designed to avoid leaving visible marks.

FOX 11 reported that prosecutors allege Xuan and Zhang actively monitored and directed nannies to subject the children to daily beatings using sticks hidden throughout the house. Children were also allegedly coached to deny being beaten.
SURROGATE, CALIFORNIA COUPLE CLASH IN COURT AS NEWBORN FIGHTS FOR LIFE AFTER HEART SURGERY

In one documented instance, Xuan allegedly instructed a nanny who was striking a child to hit harder before joining in himself, delivering open-handed blows to the child's head, striking the child's bare buttocks and lifting the child by a single arm while continuing the assault. Another boy was forced to perform continuous squats or hold a "horse stance" position for hours as punishment.

The couple operated Future Spring Surrogacy directly from their home, recruiting surrogates and paying them tens of thousands of dollars to carry children to term. While one surrogate received $135,000, prosecutors noted that many were recruited under misleading pretenses.
American flags fly outside Arcadia City Hall in Arcadia, Calif., May 13, 2026. During the search of the home, investigators found between $8 million and $9 million in liquor. (Getty Images)
At least eight surrogates reported aggressive tactics and false statements regarding the family's living situation.

Law enforcement found evidence of vast financial resources inside the home. Xuan allegedly maintained more than 200 bank accounts, stacks of cash used to pay nannies, and passports for multiple countries, including Mexico.
Authorities also discovered between $8 million and $9 million in liquor stored inside the mansion.

Investigators are working to determine the biological and social parents of all 21 children involved. The Los Angeles County Department of Children and Family Services has taken custody of the children to oversee their long-term medical care, psychological evaluation and legal placement.
CALIFORNIA PASTOR CHARGED WITH YEARSLONG CHILD MOLESTATION AS INVESTIGATORS SEEK MORE VICTIMS: DA

"This was not a home where these children were loved and nurtured," DA Hochman said. "This was a home where these young children were systematically beaten and punished if they did not do what they were told. These alleged abusers will now face the full force of the law as we hold them accountable for their despicable actions."
The discovery was made after a child was brought to Children's Hospital Los Angeles for treatment. (AP Photo/Jae C. Hong/File)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Nanny Chunmei Li was charged with child abuse causing great bodily injury or death; authorities said she has since fled to China.
Beyond the child abuse allegations, law enforcement is probing Xuan’s past, including his connection to a property previously linked to an illegal casino and a psilocybin mushroom growing operation.
Fox News Digital reached out to attorneys for Xuan and Zhang for comment. It remains unclear how long the alleged abuse had been occurring prior to May 2025.
Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

title: Mall of America terror plot thwarted; suspected ISIS sympathizer arrested, FBI announces
summary: Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud, 18, allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS and discussed a mass shooting at the Mall of America before buying an AK-47 rifle.
story: The FBI announced the arrest of an 18-year-old Minnesota man who allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS and discussed carrying out a mass shooting at the Mall of America.

An 18-year-old Minnesota man who allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS and discussed carrying out a mass shooting at the Mall of America was arrested after buying an AK-47-style rifle, magazines and ammunition from an undercover FBI employee, according to newly filed federal court documents.

Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud had allegedly spent months discussing his desire to carry out an attack, telling an FBI confidential source in September, "I can’t wait until I kill kuffar man. October 24 is the day insha Allah," according to an affidavit filed in federal court in Minnesota.
When the source later asked why he had chosen Oct. 24, Mohamud allegedly pointed to a "Hmong Arts Celebration" at the Mall of America, saying it would have "a lot of people," the affidavit states.
WOMAN’S ALLEGED ISIS RADICALIZATION UNFOLDED ONLINE BEFORE CAPITOL BOMB PLOT: COURT DOCS

Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud, 18, was arrested after FBI officials say he allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS and discussed carrying out a mass shooting at the Mall of America.  (U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota)

"Mohamud met with someone he believed to be a loyal member of ISIS to attempt to purchase an AK-47 rifle, knowing it would be used in a felony or federal crime of terrorism," Special Agent in Charge, FBI Minneapolis Field Office, Christopher Dotson said at a press conference Wednesday. "Mohamud planned to use the gun he bought in a high-traffic public area just a few weeks' time in support of a designated foreign terrorist organization."
Mohamud is now charged with knowingly receiving a firearm and ammunition while knowing or having reasonable cause to believe they would be used to commit a felony and federal crime of terrorism.

Mohamud, who was born in the United States and is a U.S. citizen, is the son of Somali nationals who later became naturalized U.S. citizens, multiple federal law enforcement sources told Fox News Digital.

His parents arrived in the U.S. through a New York City airport in 2000, according to the sources, though it remains unclear whether they entered on visas or as refugees. His mother became a naturalized citizen in 2010 and his father in 2017.
The Mall of America in Bloomington, Minnesota. (Michael Siluk/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images, File)

FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital in a statement that the suspect "allegedly obtained a weapon he hoped to use in a mass casualty attack in support of ISIS, but this FBI arrested him and put a stop to his plans."

"Once again, this FBI is moving more effectively than we ever have before at stopping terrorists before they can attack Americans – with over 1,100 individuals prevented from conducting attacks, over 4,000 foreign terrorist organization related disruptions and arrests, a 38% increase, and more," Patel said. "We will continue to use every resource we have to detect and prevent acts of terrorism and wipe out their networks all over the country. Thank you to FBI Minneapolis, who did an outstanding job in the investigation and likely saved lives."
President Donald Trump also praised the FBI’s handling of the case while speaking to reporters Wednesday.

"I did hear about it. And they did a great job. The FBI did a great job," Trump said.Mohamud appeared before a federal judge in Minnesota on Wednesday for an eight-minute initial hearing, according to federal court records.
FBI Director Kash Patel conducts a news conference at the Department of Justice. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images, File)
U.S. Magistrate Judge Elizabeth Cowan Wright ordered Mohamud temporarily detained. He is scheduled to return to court Monday, Oct. 19, at 11 a.m. ET for a preliminary and detention hearing.

ISIS-K MILITANT SENTENCED TO 20 YEARS FOR SUPPORTING DEADLY 2021 ABBEY GATE BOMBINGMinnesota Gov. Tim Walz thanked law enforcement for acting quickly to stop the alleged plot, saying federal authorities should remain focused on preventing similar threats.

"Grateful for the swift and professional action to keep Minnesotans safe," Walz wrote in an X post. "This is exactly the kind of threat we need federal law enforcement working to prevent, and the kind of work that should remain a priority as we navigate a more dangerous world."
Mall of America said the news was unsettling for its guests, tenants, employees and the broader community while thanking the FBI and other law enforcement agencies for disrupting the alleged threat.

"We are grateful to the FBI and its law enforcement partners for their vigilance and extraordinary investigative work in identifying, disrupting and removing this threat and protecting the community we all share," Mall of America said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital.
AMY KLOBUCHAR CALLS FOR MAJOR ANTI-TERRORISM INVESTMENTS AFTER ALLEGED MALL OF AMERICA PLOT
The mall added that safety and security remain its highest priority and said it would continue working closely with local, state and federal law enforcement.

House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., also praised the FBI’s handling of the case Wednesday after Fox News senior congressional correspondent Aishah Hasnie asked him about the alleged plot during a news conference in Mason, Michigan.
"The thwarting of the planned terrorist attack in the Mall in Minnesota today was another example of how important law enforcement is to us," Johnson said.
Johnson pointed to cooperation among federal, state and local law enforcement and argued that agencies need adequate funding and public support.

"What would happen if that 18-year-old had made it into that mall? It would have been a very different outcome. So we applaud everybody involved in that investigation, all the great law enforcement officers who did their job, and we pray their safety for their safety and that they continue to do that work around the country," Johnson said.

The arrest capped an FBI investigation that began around December 2024 and eventually involved a confidential human source who communicated extensively with Mohamud over encrypted messaging and social media platforms, according to investigators.

Those conversations initially centered on Mohamud allegedly wanting to leave the United States and join al-Shabaab, the Somalia-based terrorist organization. In May, he allegedly told the source he was "so excited to make hijrah" and wanted to go to Somalia, get married and "fight the enemies of Allah." He said he planned to work for about six weeks to save $2,000 for a plane ticket, according to the affidavit.
By July, however, investigators say his plans had changed.

Mohamud allegedly told the source he did not have enough money to travel to Somalia and wrote, "so i will do attack here." He later discussed buying two pistols online and going to the Mall of America or the Minnesota State Fair around Christmas, according to the affidavit.
DENVER MAN'S ESCAPE EXPOSES CHILLING TREN DE ARAGUA KIDNAPPING PLOT THAT LANDS TRIO IN PRISON

The Mall of America in Bloomington, Minnesota, left, and Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud, 18, who is accused of plotting a mass shooting at the mall in support of ISIS. (Getty Images/Sherburne County Sheriff's Office)

Mohamud allegedly discussed attacking the Mall of America with an assault rifle and told the source he could "drive straight to the crowded place and start shooting." In September, investigators say he also sent the source a selfie-style video pledging allegiance to ISIS and its leader.

The FBI then arranged an undercover weapons transaction. On Sept. 25, the source told Mohamud a "brother" could sell him an AK-style rifle, magazines and ammunition, and Mohamud allegedly indicated he wanted the weapon to be fully automatic.

On Tuesday, Mohamud met the supposed ISIS-connected "brother" — actually an undercover FBI employee — and allegedly paid $600 for an AK-47-style rifle, four magazines and roughly 200 rounds of ammunition. The rifle had been rendered inoperable, though the ammunition was live. During the meeting, Mohamud allegedly said he planned to carry out a shooting at a "kuffar festival" at the Mall of America.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Mohamud left the vehicle with the rifle, magazines and ammunition in a duffel bag and was arrested at gunpoint by FBI agents, according to the affidavit.

title: Nolan Wells' friends sue Terrell Owens for defamation after he demanded their arrests
summary: Three friends of Nolan Wells filed a defamation lawsuit against Terrell Owens over his X post demanding their arrest after the student's death.
story: Fox News' Kayleigh McEnany conducts an exclusive interview with Jax Pitalo, Warren Hudson and Morgan Seymour, the friends of Nolan Wells. They discuss the July 4 boat emergency near Horn Island. They also address the grand jury report and the shocking death threats they received.

Three friends of Nolan Wells, the college student who disappeared from a Fourth of July celebration on a Mississippi island and was later found dead, have sued former NFL star Terrell Owens for defamation.
The friends — Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo and Morgan Seymour — accused the Hall of Fame wide receiver of defaming them after he posted on X: "ARREST THEM IMMEDIATELY!!"
The fathers of the three friends filed the federal lawsuit on their sons' behalf Monday. All three are under 21, making them minors under Mississippi law.

Hudson, Pitalo and Seymour were among a large group of friends who traveled by boat with 18-year-old Wells to Horn Island on the Fourth of July. The three all said Wells did not return to mainland Mississippi with the group because he was talking to a girl, an account his family has disputed. Wells' body was found two days later off the island's coast.

Morgan Seymour, left, Warren Hudson, center, and Jax Pitalo, right, all friends of Nolan Wells, sued Terrell Owens on Oct. 5, 2026, for allegedly defaming them on social media. ("Saturday in America"/Screengrab)
NOLAN WELLS' FRIENDS CLEARED BY GRAND JURY AS THEIR LAWYERS VOW TO HOLD ONLINE ACCUSERS ACCOUNTABLE

Images showing Wells, who was Black, with his white friends before his disappearance circulated widely online, with some social media users viewing the circumstances surrounding his death through a racial lens and directing suspicion toward his friends.

Owens joined the public criticism in a Sept. 26 post that remains online. The post links to an Instagram reel by content creator Trent Out Loud that accused the three young men of deleting Snapchat messages from Wells' phone after his death while also suggesting they may have been responsible for killing him.

However, Andrew Garrett, a digital forensics expert hired by attorney Benjamin Crump, examined Wells' phone and concluded that no one accessed it between 2:18 p.m. on July 4, when Wells last unlocked it, and 3:14 a.m. on July 5, when his parents gained access to the device.
Garrett also clarified that Snapchat messages can disappear from a recipient's phone when they are remotely deleted by the person who sent them.

Nolan Wells smiles on the field while playing wide receiver for Southwest Mississippi Community College. Wells was found dead off the coast of Horn Island after disappearing during a Fourth of July celebration. (Christine Wonsley/Facebook)
'THE WIND AND DRIFT PATTERNS TELL A STORY,' CAJUN NAVY OFFICIAL SAYS OF MISSING MISSISSIPPI TEEN FOUND DEAD
In the lawsuit, the friends say Owens, 52, circulated a false narrative about them and accused them of crimes they did not commit.

"The Defamatory X Post also placed Warren, Jax, and Morgan before Owens’ audience in a false light, as murderers and participants in a murder coverup who had escaped justice," according to the lawsuit. "There was absolutely no evidence to prompt an arrest of the Plaintiffs because they had done nothing wrong, and there was no probable cause to arrest Plaintiffs because they had not committed a crime."
Owens and SMAC Entertainment, which lists him as a client on its website, did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

title: DHS orders deportation of illegal migrant who sold fraudulent DHS, FBI 'immunity' cards
summary: A Brazilian illegal immigrant created a fake DHS branch and sold counterfeit Department of Homeland Security and FBI IDs promising deportation immunity.
story: Central District of California U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli discusses the latest on the federal government's arrest of four illegal immigrants accused of running a Social Security fraud ring, the scope of the alleged scheme, and the Trump administration's ongoing efforts to crack down on fraud and illegal immigration on 'America Reports.'

FIRST ON FOX: A Brazilian illegal immigrant who admitted to creating a fake branch of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and selling counterfeit DHS and FBI identification cards — which he claimed would provide immunity from federal immigration officers — has been ordered deported.

Mario Cesar Dos Santos Jr., 50, who entered the United States in 2016 and overstayed his visa, is currently in removal proceedings, according to DHS. He was arrested in February at Orlando International Airport after arriving on a flight from Boston.
Dos Santos pleaded guilty to wire fraud and the fraudulent use of government seals.
WOMAN EXPOSED RUNNING VISA FRAUD SCHEME SPANNING YEARS, POSING AS IMMIGRATION OFFICER

Mario Cesar Dos Santos Jr., 50, is accused of operating a sham organization called the "Chaplain Emergency Management Agency" and charging $400 per person for bogus training courses that generated about $14,000. (Middle District of Florida U.S. Attorney’s Office Case #5:26cr17, USA v. Dos Santos)

As part of the scheme, Dos Santos claimed to be the president of the "Chaplain Emergency Management Agency" (CEMA), a fictitious federal agency he created to trick attendees at training seminars into paying for immunity from immigration enforcement.

While the training courses were offered for free, participants were charged $400 to $450 for bogus certificates they believed would protect them from deportation, authorities said. Each seminar drew approximately 30 to 45 participants.
FORMER USCIS OFFICIAL, ACCOMPLICE CHARGED IN ALLEGED $960K CITIZENSHIP BRIBERY SCHEME

Prosecutors say the fake certificates featured unauthorized DHS and FBI seals, leading to the arrest of Mario Cesar Dos Santos, Jr., 50, in Florida after an investigation by DHS, the FBI and FEMA. Santos, an illegal immigrant from Brazil, now faces deportation, in addition to prison time. (PKevin Carter/Getty Images; Middle District of Florida U.S. Attorney’s Office Case #5:26cr17, USA v. Dos Santos)

In addition to the counterfeit certificates, Dos Santos sold clothing, badges, stickers and other merchandise bearing official seals for DHS and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) — the agency responsible for coordinating federal responses to natural and human-made disasters.
A confidential informant purchased several of these items at a training seminar last year, according to authorities.
TRUMP ADMIN’S FRAUD CRACKDOWN TARGETS FOREIGNERS ACCUSED OF INFILTRATING US FEDERAL PROGRAMS

Prosecutors say the fake certificates featured unauthorized DHS and FBI seals, leading to his arrest in Ocala after an investigation by DHS, the FBI and FEMA. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images; Middle District of Florida U.S. Attorney’s Office Case #5:26cr17, USA v. Dos Santos)

The CEMA website, its social media accounts and a group chat — which had more than 750 members when the investigation launched in August 2025 — actively promoted upcoming courses and displayed an altered DHS seal, authorities said.
The organization also falsely claimed to be accredited by the International Association for Continuing Education and the American Council on Education.
Dos Santos faces up to 20 years in federal prison when he is sentenced on Dec. 18.

title: Bar named in Cornell rape lawsuit disputes accuser's account, says she was never served alcohol while underage
summary: An Ithaca, New York, bar disputed the Cornell University gang-rape accuser's claim it served her alcohol underage on the night of the alleged Chi Phi assault.
story: Fox News national correspondent Bryan Llenas joins 'Fox & Friends' to report the latest on Cornell University's handling of a sexual assault investigation as students protest and call for resignations.

A bar named in the lawsuit at the center of the Cornell University sexual assault firestorm is disputing the alleged victim's claim that it served her alcohol while she was underage on the night of the alleged assault — a denial the bar has now also lodged in court.

Moonies Bar & Nightclub, a downtown Ithaca, New York, bar popular with Cornell students, told Fox News that underage guests at a private Tri Delta sorority event on Oct. 19, 2024, were marked on their hands, while guests over 21 received wristbands. The bar says its bartenders served alcohol only to guests wearing wristbands.
The complaint and Moonies' account both say Doe was marked as underage. They differ over whether she was then served alcohol.

Doe's lawsuit alleges a Moonies bouncer placed an "X" on each of the then-20-year-old's hands to signify she was under 21, but that she was nevertheless served and consumed at least one alcoholic beverage inside the bar.
INSIDE EXPLOSIVE CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS: 7 MEN ACCUSED, CONFLICTING ACCOUNTS AND A POLITICAL FIRESTORM
The Chi Phi fraternity house stands on the Cornell University campus in Ithaca, N.Y., on Oct. 2, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images)
"No alcohol was served to anyone who had mark on their hands," Moonies said in a statement to Fox News Tuesday, disputing the allegations.
CORNELL PRESIDENT SAYS UNIVERSITY 'MUST DO BETTER' ON HANDLING OF SEXUAL ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS
Moonies also told Fox News that Doe later worked for the company from February to March 2025 and discussed the October 2024 incident during that period.
According to the bar, Doe never said during those conversations that she had been intoxicated at Moonies or served alcohol by one of its bartenders.
Fox News Digital contacted Doe's attorney for a response to both of Moonies' assertions.

In a formal answer filed Sunday in New York Supreme Court, Zareen Enterprises LLC, which does business as Moonies Bar & Nightclub, denied unlawfully selling or furnishing alcohol to anyone under the legal drinking age and denied selling or furnishing alcohol to any visibly intoxicated person.

The filing specifically denies the paragraph of Doe's complaint alleging she was served alcohol at Moonies despite having been marked as underage. Moonies also denied that any act or omission on its part caused Doe's alleged injuries.
The bar asked the court to dismiss the complaint against it in its entirety.
General view of Moonies Bar and Nightclub in Ithaca, N.Y., Tuesday October 7, 2026. (Richard Beetham for Fox News Digital)

The dispute comes as the case has roiled Cornell and drawn national attention, with thousands rallying on campus Monday and faculty senators now pushing a no-confidence resolution against the university's central administration over its handling of sexual assault. Gov. Kathy Hochul has also appointed the New York Attorney General's Office as special prosecutor, with Attorney General Letitia James leading an "active criminal investigation."
Moonies said it hosted the private Tri Delta event from 9 p.m. to 11 p.m. that night with about 185 guests, including roughly 150 who were over 21 and 35 who were underage.
The bar said it had a contract with the sorority and marked underage guests' hands while providing wristbands to those over 21.

In the statement, Moonies called Doe's allegation that she was served alcohol "completely inaccurate," saying its employees "strictly followed the rules and did not serve alcohol to any underaged guests."
WATCH: CORNELL STUDENTS PROTEST SCHOOL'S HANDLING OF SEXUAL ASSAULT INVESTIGATION:
CORNELL PICKS FORMER DEPUTY US ATTORNEY GENERAL TO REVIEW SEX ASSAULT RESPONSE

In its court filing, Moonies also asserted as affirmative defenses that Doe cannot establish that it unlawfully sold alcohol to an underage or visibly intoxicated person, or that any alleged unlawful sale caused her injuries. The bar maintained that it complied with all applicable laws and regulations governing alcohol sales.
The dispute concerns one part of Doe's account of the hours preceding the alleged assault and what happened at Moonies before she arrived at Chi Phi.

According to her lawsuit, Doe began the evening drinking vodka at her Tri Delta sorority house before a sorority housemother accompanied her to Moonies. She later went to another Ithaca bar before leaving alone around 11 p.m. and walking to the Chi Phi fraternity house to meet a friend who was a member.
By the time she arrived at Chi Phi, Doe was visibly intoxicated and had consumed roughly 10 standard drinks over three hours, according to her complaint.

Once inside, Doe alleges she was given another beer before going upstairs, where two fraternity members pressured her into snorting what they said was ketamine, a drug she says she had never previously taken. She alleges they also gave her marijuana and high-proof liquor before sexual activity began.

Doe alleges other fraternity members became involved as the night progressed and that she eventually became "completely incapacitated." Seven former Chi Phi fraternity brothers are accused in her lawsuit of sexual assault and rape.
Students protest in Ho Plaza at Cornell University, Monday, October 5, 2026, in Ithaca, New York, in response to an alleged sexual assault in 2024. (Richard Beetham for Fox News Digital)
The men have denied wrongdoing, with some maintaining that sexual activity was consensual and others denying they participated. No criminal charges have been filed against the seven men.
The case burst into public view when Doe filed the 101-page lawsuit Sept. 16, nearly two years after the alleged encounter.

In addition to the seven former fraternity members, Doe sued Cornell University, Chi Phi and affiliated entities, her own Tri Delta sorority and Moonies, among others, alleging that institutions around her failed to protect her before, during and after the events of that night.

Students protest on Ho Plaza at Cornell University on Monday, Oct. 5, 2026, in Ithaca, N.Y., in response to an alleged sexual assault in 2024 involving members of the Chi Phi fraternity. (Richard Beetham for Fox News Digital)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The lawsuit's allegations prompted renewed scrutiny of the original criminal investigation.

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, who initially declined to pursue charges, has said the six-page sworn statement his office received from Cornell University Police in 2024 did not allege that Doe was drugged against her will or gang-raped and instead described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as "voluntary, conscious, and consensual."

A fuller transcript of Doe's November 2024 police interviews later obtained by CBS New York included statements in which she distinguished the initial sexual encounter from later activity and explicitly told investigators she had been raped.
Van Houten said his office had never received that transcript.
Fox News' Michelle Langer contributed to this report.

title: Man pleads guilty to 2023 killing of Lauren Heike on Phoenix hiking trail
summary: Zion Teasley admitted to killing Lauren Heike, whose body was found with 15 stab wounds along a north Phoenix, Arizona, community trail in 2023.
story: Phoenix Police officials say they have arrested a man in connection with an attack at a North Phoenix hiking trail that killed 29-year-old Lauren Heike. (FOX 10)
Zion Teasley has pleaded guilty to the 2023 murder of Lauren Heike, who was found dead with multiple stab wounds along a trail in north Phoenix.

Teasley entered the plea last Friday to first-degree premeditated murder, as well as a separate sexual exploitation of a minor charge stemming from conduct dating to 2019, according to the Maricopa County Superior Court. Under the plea agreement, Teasley is expected to be sentenced to natural life in prison, and prosecutors will withdraw their pursuit of the death penalty. His sentencing is scheduled for Dec. 4.
He was also charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and first-degree burglary in 2020, but prosecutors voluntarily dismissed those charges last week as part of the plea agreement.

In the aftermath of Heike's killing, a police report revealed that Teasley had been struggling with his sexuality and gender identity, ABC 15 said. Police previously said they believed Heike's killing was a random attack, and investigators found no prior communication between Heike and Teasley, according to the outlet. He was also a former Marine recruit who was separated from recruit training just months after enlisting in 2019, the outlet said.
PHOENIX WOMAN, 29, FOUND DEAD ON HIKING TRAIL
Heike was found with 15 stab wounds after investigators said she was chased along a Phoenix trail. (Maricopa County Sheriff's Office / Phoenix Police Department)

"Our records indicate that Zion W. Teasley entered recruit training at Marine Corps Recruit Training Depot San Diego on March 25, 2019. He was separated June 17, 2019, prior to completing boot camp," the U.S. Marine Corps told the outlet.

When questioned by the police, Teasley said Heike appeared to be "what I would want to look like," according to the outlet.Investigators also uncovered a screenshot that they believed shed light on Teasley's state of mind. It read, "When I see a beautiful woman, and I'm a man," ABC 15 said.
The outlet added that Teasley was fired from one of his jobs for being "aggressive toward female employees" and was "suspected of stealing merchandise."
PHOENIX POLICE ARREST SUSPECT IN CONNECTION TO LAUREN HEIKE'S DEATH
Lauren Heike, 29, was found dead along a community hiking trail in Phoenix in 2023. (Phoenix Police Department)
Heike was killed in April 2023 when a resident found her body along a community trail, officials said. She was found with 15 stab wounds and injuries to her hands and forearms, police reported.
Investigators said DNA, surveillance video and cellphone location evidence linked Teasley to the crime.

Heike's family said they had supported prosecutors' initial decision to seek the death penalty but ultimately agreed with the plea agreement, which ensures Teasley will spend the rest of his life in prison without the possibility of release.
Detectives said surveillance footage captured a person who may be connected to Lauren Heike’s death. (Phoenix Police Department)

Based on the condition of Heike's clothes and officials finding her belongings scattered along the trail, investigators believe Heike was chased over a barbed wire fence during the attack.
"The suspect ran after Lauren and then sprinted away before returning to the location where Lauren's body was found and climbing over the barbed wire," Teasley's probable cause statement read.

title: Denver man’s escape exposes chilling Tren de Aragua kidnapping plot that lands trio in prison

Darwin Veliz-Gonzalez, Jefferson Balza-Delfin and Yender Enrique Campos-Malave, all Venezuelan nationals, were each sentenced to 20 years in federal prison for the kidnapping and torture, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Colorado announced.
A fourth defendant’s sentencing was postponed.
BIDEN ‘MADNESS’ STILL BEING REVEALED AS FATHER KILLED, CHILDREN KIDNAPPED BY TERROR GROUP MEMBER: DOJ

"This is what Tren de Aragua was doing in our community," U.S. Attorney Peter McNeilly said. "Colorado is safer with these violent criminals in federal prison for the next 20 years, and we will continue to pursue every member of Tren de Aragua until there are no more left in our state."
The victim had been renting a room in the Denver home, when his roommates learned that he and his father were police officers in Venezuela and took him captive, prosecutors said.
They tied him up with rope and held him for several days without food and with very little water.
SIX MEN ALLEGEDLY KIDNAPPED TWO PEOPLE AT VACATION RESORT, TORTURED THEM AT BOAT RAMP: FBI

Federal prosecutors announced that three Venezuelan nationals each received 20-year prison sentences for kidnapping and torturing their Denver roommate in a ransom plot carried out for Tren de Aragua. (U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Colorado)

During that time, the men filmed themselves strangling him with a rope until he nearly lost consciousness, repeatedly holding his head in a bucket of water for 30 seconds or longer, threatening him with a gun and pistol-whipping him.
They sent the recordings to his wife to demand ransom from his family in Venezuela and shared them with international TdA leaders, whom they consulted about the kidnapping, prosecutors said.
When the family did not pay, one gang leader explicitly suggested cutting off a finger to pressure them into sending money.

The victim had been renting a room in a Denver home, when his roommates learned that he and his father were police officers in Venezuela. (Dave Parsons via iStock, File)
The victim heard his captors discussing the plan before Balza-Delfin used pliers to sever his right pinky finger, an act the men also filmed.

Denver police came to the South Hazel Court home on Oct. 16, 2024, after receiving a welfare call reporting that someone had been kidnapped there. After the visit, three of the men fled the residence, giving the victim an opportunity to escape. He walked into a Denver police station the next morning, reported the kidnapping and assault and showed officers his missing finger.
Denver police investigated the kidnapping and torture of a man by his roommates in a ransom plot carried out for Tren de Aragua, federal prosecutors said. (Denver Police Department)
Denver Police Chief Ron Thomas praised the victim for coming forward.

"I applaud the victim of this heinous crime, and all victims, regardless of immigration status, for reporting criminal behaviors and helping us arrest those who prey on our community members," Thomas said.
A federal grand jury has separately indicted Brawins Dominique Suarez Villegas, also known as "Chino San Vicente," for his alleged role in the kidnapping and torture.
PATEL SAYS FBI IS 'MANHUNTING' TERROR SUSPECTS AROUND THE GLOBE AFTER TWO HIGH-VALUE CAPTURES

An armed crew of nine suspected Tren de Aragua gang members were caught on camera wreaking havoc at a Colorado apartment complex, in an incident Aurora police are calling "very reminiscent" of what the city experienced at another apartment building last summer. (Aurora Police)
He is also accused of participating in a broader TdA criminal operation involving robbery, extortion, kidnapping, money laundering and drug crimes between May 2024 and approximately March 2025.

A former St. Louis television news anchor who admitted to fatally stabbing her mother in Kansas last Halloween has been sentenced to life in prison.
Angelynn "Angie" Mock, 48, will be eligible for parole after 25 years, according to a Sedgwick County District Court judge, KWCH reported.
The ruling comes after Mock reached a plea agreement in the case, in which she was charged with first-degree murder.
TEEN PLANNED MIDDLE SCHOOL MASSACRE BEFORE MAKING DEADLY ‘LAST-MINUTE CHOICE’ TO KILL MOM: OFFICIAL
Former St. Louis television news anchor Angelynn "Angie" Mock has been charged with first-degree murder following the fatal stabbing of her mother in Wichita, Kansas. (Angie Mock/Facebook)
On the morning of Oct. 31, 2025, officers discovered Anita Avers, 80, with several stab wounds inside her Wichita, Kansas, home, which she shared with Mock and Mock’s stepfather.
According to a probable cause affidavit, Mock made several statements suggesting she believed her mother was the devil and that she killed her to "save herself."
Mock’s stepfather told KAKE-TV that she had been diagnosed with mental illness and suffers from delusions and depression.
KWCH added that Mock’s stepfather said she may have suffered from bipolar disorder, which was later believed to be schizoaffective disorder.
Angelynn "Angie" Mock pleaded guilty to first-degree murder for the Halloween 2025 stabbing death of her mother. (Angie Mock/Facebook | Sedgwick County Jail)

Despite those claims, a judge found Mock competent to stand trial in July.

title: Mother accused of trying to kill daughters in freeway crash and knife attack as soldiers step in
summary: Two Joint Base Lewis-McChord soldiers tackled and disarmed a mother who allegedly stabbed a 9-year-old girl after a violent SUV crash on Interstate 5.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A Washington state mother accused of trying to kill her daughters with a knife and a freeway crash now faces attempted murder charges after soldiers and another bystander stepped in to stop the alleged attack.

Janieka Amber Marie Ellington, 35, faces four counts of attempted first-degree murder, two counts of vehicular assault and one count of felony harassment involving threats to kill, according to Pierce County Superior Court records.
Prosecutors allege she tried to kill the girls both by stabbing or cutting them and by crashing their vehicle, according to charging documents.

The case stems from Monday morning’s rollover wreck on southbound Interstate 5 near DuPont, where witnesses said Ellington chased her teenage daughter with a knife and threatened to kill her after the crash, FOX 13 Seattle reported.
WATCH: BYSTANDERS, POLICE LIFT VOLKSWAGEN OFF WOMAN PINNED UNDERNEATH AFTER DRAMATIC E-BIKE CRASH

Bystanders assist at the scene of a rollover crash on Interstate 5 near DuPont, Wash., Monday. Two soldiers reportedly restrained a woman accused of stabbing a 9-year-old girl after the crash. (Nathan Wilkinson)
Three bystanders, including two soldiers, disarmed Ellington and restrained her until Washington State Patrol troopers arrived, the outlet reported.
"I just did my part," Sgt. Ricardo A. Nunez, a 7th Infantry Division soldier stationed at Joint Base Lewis-McChord, said, according to FOX 13.
"I am glad I was there to help those girls and was just in the right place at the right time."
Court records show a judge ordered a competency evaluation Tuesday. A competency hearing is scheduled for Oct. 20.
Troopers responded shortly before 9 a.m. Monday to reports of an SUV driving erratically near mile marker 118, according to FOX 13.

In its initial report, the outlet stated that the SUV struck a concrete barrier, veered toward the right shoulder and then crossed back into traffic, hitting a semi-truck. It struck the barrier again and rolled over near Center Drive, Exit 118.
SOUTH CAROLINA WOMAN ACCUSED OF STABBING LYFT DRIVER 11 TIMES CLAIMS MENTAL HEALTH CRISIS
Military service members assist an overturned SUV on Interstate 5 near DuPont, Wash., Monday. (Nathan Wilkinson)

Ellington told hospital staff and troopers she had been drinking whiskey the night before and was driving without sleep, according to court records. One of her daughters told investigators Ellington believed people were following them before the crash.
A 9-year-old girl suffered multiple broken bones and a stab wound, while a 15-year-old girl was hospitalized without serious injuries, according to the outlet.
Witness Nathan Wilkinson told KING 5 he was driving to work when he came upon the wreck and saw two men in military uniforms from Joint Base Lewis-McChord intervene.

"There's people standing around, then all of a sudden there was a flash, and then the two soldiers jumped on a person. … I heard a scream at that time," Wilkinson told the outlet. "I saw one of the soldiers had a knife in his hand that he had dislodged from the person they tackled."
FLORIDA MAN ARRESTED FOR DUI AFTER TROOPERS ALLEGEDLY FIND 34 OPEN ALCOHOL CONTAINERS IN VEHICLE
Washington State Patrol says the woman allegedly threatened two girls with a knife following Monday morning’s crash near DuPont, Wash. (Washington State Patrol)
Wilkinson called 911 as bystanders subdued the woman, KING 5 reported.

The attempted murder charges include two counts alleging Ellington intended to kill by stabbing or cutting and two alleging she intended to kill through a vehicle crash, according to the charging documents.

Prosecutors also alleged domestic violence and aggravating circumstances, including that Ellington used a position of trust to facilitate the offenses and that the victims were particularly vulnerable or unable to resist.
ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT SUSPECT CHARGED IN CRASH THAT KILLED POLICE OFFICER AND HIS GIRLFRIEND

An entrance plaque at Joint Base Lewis-McChord in Pierce County, Wash. Two service members reportedly intervened after a woman allegedly stabbed a child following a rollover crash on a nearby freeway Monday. (Facebook/Joint Base Lewis-McChord)
Wilkinson said he hoped the service members would be recognized for stopping to help.

title: Transgender Washington state resident accused of fueling deadly Canadian school massacre that killed 8: DOJ
summary: James Cody Bryant allegedly sent money, offered advice and agreed to livestream the Tumbler Ridge school shooting instead of alerting law enforcement.
story: Federal officials say James Cody Bryant sent money, offered advice and agreed to livestream the Canadian school shooting that killed eight victims. (Credit: U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Washington)

A transgender Washington state resident allegedly helped fuel a Canadian school massacre that left children dead, choosing to aid the shooter, who also identified as a transgender, instead of sounding the alarm, federal officials said Tuesday.

James Cody Bryant, 30, was arrested Tuesday morning in Bellingham north of Seattle, accused of sending money, offering advice and agreeing to broadcast the Feb. 10 attack at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School in British Columbia.

"Bryant had the information and ability to alert law enforcement, and even discussed that possibility with the shooter, but he chose not to," Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd said at a Seattle news conference.
"Instead, he encouraged and offered assistance to a murderer."
TRANSGEDNER EX-STUDENT IDENTIFIED AS ALLEGED SUSPECT IN DEADLY CANADA SCHOOL MASS SHOOTING

U.S. and Canadian officials discuss the arrest of James Cody Bryant, 30, in connection with the deadly Tumbler Ridge school shooting during a news conference Tuesday in Seattle. (U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Washington)

Bryant faces a federal charge of conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country. Prosecutors allege Bryant helped the shooter, 18-year-old Jesse Van Rootselaar, start a car to reach the school after the killings had begun.

"So even after the shooter had already tragically killed two family members, Bryant assisted the shooter in successfully traveling to the second location to take even more lives," FBI Seattle Special Agent in Charge W. Mike Herrington said.
"In the complaint, Bryant even admits to being maybe the only one who could stop the shooter."
Herrington confirmed that Bryant and Van Rootselaar both identified as transgender, and said Bryant identifies as female.
The two met through a random pairing on the online chat service Omegle roughly three years before the attack.
Investigators have no indication what their transgender identities were, why they remained in contact, or that they ever met in person, Herrington said.
TEEN PLANNED MIDDLE SCHOOL MASSACRE BEFORE MAKING DEADLY ‘LAST-MINUTE CHOICE’ TO KILL MOM: OFFICIAL

Police tape surrounds the Tumbler Ridge Secondary School and other buildings in Tumbler Ridge, Vancouver, British Columbia, Feb. 11, the day after a mass shooting there. (Jesse Boily /The Canadian Press via AP, File)
Their online friendship developed into discussions of violence over at least six months, according to Herrington.
"This complaint was particularly difficult to read, in part because of the casual tone these two individuals used when discussing the mass taking of innocent lives that was being planned," he said.
Bryant allegedly agreed to record and broadcast a livestream to maximize the shooter’s notoriety.
"Bryant even stayed awake after an overnight work shift to make sure this horrific act could be widely viewed online," Herrington said.
FLORIDA MAN INDICTED FOR ALLEGEDLY PLOTTING MASS SHOOTING TARGETING JEWISH EMPLOYEES AT ADVOCACY ORGANIZATION

Police officers and investigators work outside Tumbler Ridge Secondary School, where a mass shooting took place in the small town of Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, Canada, on Feb. 10. (Eagle Vision Agency / AFP via Getty Images, File)

"We certainly know the shooter was concerned that not enough people would see the livestream without Bryant broadcasting it, and was depending on Bryant to amplify the livestream because the shooter did not have many followers on social media."

Floyd said the attempted livestream on Twitch lasted about 20 seconds before shutting down. Herrington said investigators do not know whether Van Rootselaar would have carried out the attack without Bryant’s willingness to operate it.
Officials also described financial assistance, including a little more than $100 for shoes. An attempted transfer of roughly $15 for a lighter was ultimately reversed.
NAVY VETERAN AMONG TRIO WHO ALLEGEDLY WANTED TO BEHEAD SOLDIER AND FUND ISIS DRONE ATTACKS ON AMERICANS

Community members mourn during a candlelight vigil for the victims of Tumbler Ridge Secondary School, where a mass shooting took place in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, Feb. 10. (Paige Taylor White / AFP via Getty Images, File)

Floyd said Bryant and the shooter discussed sending weapons to Canada, but Bryant was uncomfortable doing so. Herrington said investigators had no indication the guns used in the attack came from the U.S.
Asked about a possible political ideology or group affiliation, Floyd said investigators had no information indicating either.

Herrington pointed to the shooter’s suffering and "a very keen focus on notoriety" as themes in the communications. The pair discussed other mass shootings, how the public reacted and a desire for the Tumbler Ridge attack to receive similar attention, he said.

The investigation crossed the border within days of the massacre, when Canadian police received information from an online platform used by the shooter and contacted the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), British Columbia RCMP Assistant Commissioner Elija Rain said.
Floyd said investigators obtained subpoenas and warrants and reviewed thousands of communications, many on Discord, before making the arrest.
Canadian investigators have reviewed more than 90 statements from students, educators and first responders and continue to examine other online contacts, Rain said.
GEORGIA HIGH SCHOOL SHOOTING SUSPECT COLT GRAY CHANGES PLEA TO GUILTY, NOW FACES LIFE IN PRISON
A screengrab from a video shows students exiting the Tumbler Ridge school after deadly shootings, in British Columbia, Canada, Feb. 10. (Jordon Kosik via AP, File)
"Our RCMP criminal investigation remains ongoing and the possibility of further charges being pursued in Canada remains under active consideration," he said.
Herrington warned that assisting a mass shooting from afar does not shield someone from prosecution.
"If you think you are safe from prosecution because you did not pull the trigger, or were not physically present at the scene of the crime, think again," he said.

"The FBI and our partners will use all of the considerable investigative tools at our disposal to hold accountable those who enable or assist in acts of mass violence."

The Feb. 10 attack killed eight victims, including five students, an educator and the shooter’s mother and 11-year-old stepbrother, according to Canadian authorities. Van Rootselaar was found dead inside the school from an apparent self-inflicted injury.
