title: Trump dominates the Iowa Senate debate from afar
summary: Republican Ashley Hinson and Democrat Josh Turek sparred about how to handle the president and other issues in a battleground debate Wednesday night.
story: President Donald Trump was the main character in a televised Iowa Senate debate Wednesday night between Democrat Josh Turek, a state representative, and Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson.

Turek hammered Hinson for supporting Trump policies that he says are the culprit in rising costs for Iowa families — from “chaotic tariffs” to the war in Iran — whether they live in cities or on farms.

“The real issue is that Iowans are hurting, and they’re hurting uniquely,” Turek said. “I’m hearing ‘I’m struggling to keep food on the table, I’m struggling to pay my electric bill, I’m struggling to keep a roof above my head,’ and now with this war in Iran, ‘I’m struggling just to keep gas in my tank.’” He noted that Hinson voted seven times against curtailing the war and five times against reining in Trump’s tariffs.
Hinson fired back, accusing Turek of skipping out on votes in the Legislature, being “too liberal” for the state and lying when he accused her of using her position to enrich her family.

“It’s one thing to vote like an East Coast liberal; it’s another to lie like them,” she said. At another point, she jabbed Turek for flip-flopping on his willingness to legislate with Trump. “You trashed the president during the primary, and now you’re doing ads saying you’re going to work with him,” she said. “It’s a tale of two Tureks.”

But by modern standards, the debate over a Senate seat that is one of a handful that will determine party control of the chamber was unusually civil. Hinson expressed her sympathy over Turek’s sister’s being diagnosed with cancer, and Turek nodded to the pain negative ads caused both candidates. And both of them pledged to work with Trump or a future Democratic president.

“You work with the person who’s going to sign the bills, no matter who that person is, on things that are important to your state, and that’s exactly what I’ve done,” Hinson said. In particular, she pointed to laws President Joe Biden signed on preventing stillbirths and providing mental health services to rural veterans for which she was the lead Republican sponsor in the House.

Recent polls have found the race is more or less a dead heat, with several surveys showing each candidate with a lead within the margin of error. Iowa has been a reliably Republican state in recent years, with Trump having won it in all three of his bids for the presidency and the GOP controlling both Senate seats and all four U.S. House seats.

But Trump’s low approval ratings have been an anchor on Republican candidates in Iowa, as they have been across the country. Trump was about 1,000 miles south Wednesday night, campaigning in Texas as Hinson and Turek debated in Iowa, but he looms over virtually every contest approaching in the midterm election.

The last time Democrats won statewide federal races in Iowa was more than a decade ago, when Barack Obama carried the state in two presidential elections and when then-Sen. Tom Harkin was re-elected to a fifth term in 2008. The Senate seat is open because Sen. Joni Ernst, R-Iowa, is honoring a self-imposed promise to serve only two terms.

The one-on-one between Hinson and Turek, part of the Iowa Press debates series, was held at the local PBS studio in Johnston, about 10 miles north of Des Moines, and featured three journalists — from Iowa PBS, the Des Moines Register and The Gazette, a newspaper based in Cedar Rapids — asking questions.
Hinson and Turek sparred over taxes, Social Security and immigration, among other issues.

Hinson cited border crossings during Biden’s term as a reason Iowans should not trust Turek and Democrats on the issue, arguing that her rival supports “all the illegals.” Trump and Republicans, she said, deserve credit for clamping down on illegal immigration.
For Subscribers

“We have now sealed off the border, that just took about six months to get that done, and now we have zero crossings happening at our southern border,” she said. “So, who do you trust to fix the problem — the arsonists, the people who started the fire or the people who are cleaning up the mess?”

Turek affirmed that he would not vote to fund the Department of Homeland Security without significant changes to immigration enforcement policies, including requiring the use of body cameras and revising use-of-force standards.

“Yeah, that is my position,” he said. He added that he believes that no one wants to see “Americans shot in the street,” a reference to federal officers’ killing Renee Good and Alex Pretti during an immigration crackdown in Minnesota this year.
“What I am talking about is we can have safe and secure borders, and we need to have a pathway to earn citizenship for those that have come here legally,” Turek said.
For Subscribers

At several points, Turek accused Hinson of slashing Medicaid, Obamacare premium subsidies and food assistance funds to cut taxes for the wealthiest Americans. Hinson responded that she was proud to eliminate taxes on tips, overtime pay and Social Security checks, which were among the features of Trump’s signature “big, beautiful bill” last year.

Turek said he supports those provisions, but he also proposed eliminating the cap on Social Security taxes to keep the program solvent beyond the six-year time frame when benefits are expected to be reduced if Congress does not act. That cap currently shields income above $184,500 per year from Social Security taxes.

“I think that it is fundamentally wrong that you have every single teacher and police officer and firefighter that is paying payroll tax and Social Security tax year-round,” Turek said. “Meanwhile, you’ve got folks like Elon Musk and Bill Gates and Jeff Bezos that are paying just for the first few minutes of the year. The best way we can keep this solvent is by taking off the cap.”

Hinson countered that lifting the cap would not fully fund Social Security payouts and argued that a federal commission should be established to revamp the system and keep it solvent. Congress, which holds the actual authority to rewrite the Social Security law, would then vote on the commission’s plan.
“This is a serious issue for our seniors, and it is a promise we need to keep to them,” she said, accusing Turek of “fearmongering” on the issue.

The candidates ducked and weaved a little on the last questions posed to them. Hinson was asked whether Congress is abdicating its authority by allowing Trump to build a White House ballroom and promise to send $5,000 payments to Americans if Republicans win the House and the Senate.

“Well, speaking as someone who serves on the Appropriations Committee right now, I care very deeply about Article I of the Constitution, which is making sure that we have the power of the purse,” she said, without addressing whether Trump’s seizure of that authority is proper.
Turek declined to rule out voting to remove Trump from office if he is impeached by the House.
“I have no interest in looking at impeachment,” he said in response to a question. “I think that we need to look forward, not back.”

In a twist at a time when many Democratic Senate candidates are distancing themselves rhetorically from Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., Hinson said she could team up with him if Democrats win the majority and she wins the Iowa Senate seat.

“So, hopefully it’s not Chuck Schumer, but if it’s Chuck Schumer, I’ll work with him,” she said. “I got things across the line with [Rep.] Nancy Pelosi [D-Calif.] as speaker, so I think that shows that I can work with anyone.”

Earlier in the debate, she sought to undermine Turek’s boast that he is not taking money from corporate PACs by highlighting the Schumer-backed super PACs that have taken money from companies and spent heavily to help elect Turek.

“He is basically taking laundered corporate PAC money,” she said, challenging Turek to call for ads on his behalf to be taken down “if you don’t want to take that corporate PAC money, because that’s how it flows. It flows through people like Chuck Schumer, right to support you.”
Turek declined to denounce the political action committees backing him.

title: Trump says ‘we protect our cities’ after saying Iran could ‘take out’ Los Angeles or San Diego
summary: The president recast his earlier incendiary statements at a San Antonio rally meant to galvanize voters behind Texas Republicans ahead of the midterms.
story: After having faced fierce backlash, President Donald Trump on Wednesday sought to clean up incendiary comments he made earlier this week, when he said Iran could “take out” Los Angeles or San Diego.
Trump’s original remarks, made at a campaign rally in Nebraska, seemed to refer to what would happen if Iran had a nuclear weapon.
“They can take out a city. Let them take out Los Angeles. Let them take out San Diego,” Trump said Monday to cheers from the crowd.
He recast those remarks Wednesday night at a rally in San Antonio as he tried to explain the Iran war, saying he had “no choice” if the U.S. were to keep Iran from developing a nuclear weapon.
“You want to see problems? And I said it the other day: Let them hit a missile into San Diego or Los Angeles on the way. Let them hit. You want to see a horror show? You want to see problems?”
“Let them hit San Diego. Let them hit Los Angeles if you want to see some bad things happen. You want to see a country that would be in free fall?”
This time, however, he added: “We’re not going to let that happen. We protect our cities. We protect our country. We’re not letting that happen.”
For Subscribers

Trump’s initial remarks sparked backlash, particularly from California Democrats. Gov. Gavin Newsom accused Trump of prodding foreign enemies to take out U.S. cities. “He is deranged and dangerous,” Newsom wrote on social media.

“To do that makes us look ridiculous on the world stage, but it also gives a green light to Iran, the nation that he chose to attack, the green light to attack our cities,” Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass told NBC News after Wednesday’s rally.
For Subscribers
Bass said she may call on Congress to investigate Trump’s comments.

Trump’s comments Wednesday came in a winding speech at a boisterous rally that stretched for about an hour and 45 minutes, with numerous interruptions from protesters. At one point, a protester who had been heckling Trump was grabbed by a person in the audience in an incident captured on video. A man in the crowd, wearing what looked to be a red “Make America Great Again” hat, grabbed the protester by the hair. Others in the crowd tried to free the protester.
Add to Google
Add to Google

The evening was meant to boost Texas Republicans, including Attorney General Ken Paxton, who is running for the Senate in a pitched battle against Democrat James Talarico. In a reflection of Trump’s low favorability ratings, even in the red state of Texas, Gov. Greg Abbott — a staunch Trump ally — said he could not attend because of a scheduling conflict.
Capping the night, Trump announced that he would award former Major League Baseball pitcher and seven-time Cy Young Award winner Rogers Clemens the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

“We’re giving him the Presidential Medal of Freedom, and along with the Congressional Medal of Honor, it’s the highest award bestowed upon anyone,” Trump said, adding he would help him get into the Baseball Hall of Fame someday. “He deserves it.”
Clemens, a Texan, was accused of using performance-enhancing drugs late in his baseball career. He maintains he has never used PEDs.
On Wednesday night, Clemens took the stage at Trump’s invitation, saying he was “stunned.”
“This supersedes anything that obviously I’ve done in my playing career,” Clemens said. “To get it from this man, this president, there wouldn’t be another president I’d want to get it from.”

title: FDA says it will complete safety review of abortion pill in March
summary: A federal judge in Louisiana ordered the agency to provide an update on its safety study as part of a lawsuit seeking to overturn a provision allowing mifepristone to be delivered by mail.
story: The Food and Drug Administration expects to complete its safety review of the abortion pill mifepristone in March, according to a court document the Justice Department filed Wednesday.

In the filing, the FDA said it plans to compare mifepristone’s safety to that of surgical abortions through 10 weeks’ gestation. Its review will measure the frequency of side effects among roughly 100,000 women who took mifepristone, it said.
Results of the FDA’s review are expected in mid-December. From there, the agency will analyze the data and draft a final report — a process it expects to wrap up in March.
The FDA approved mifepristone in 2000, and hundreds of peer-reviewed studies have found it to be safe and effective.

The FDA temporarily eliminated a requirement to dispense mifepristone in person in 2021, then finalized the change in 2023. It said Wednesday that it plans to re-evaluate that decision based on the new data it collects. It may weigh the views of patients, providers and pharmacists, as well as additional studies it did not consider in 2023.
The review’s expected completion date falls months after the Nov. 3 midterm elections — when abortion access is among the concerns for voters.
The update Wednesday is in response to an order by a federal judge in Louisiana for a progress report on the safety review.

The FDA is a defendant in a Louisiana suit challenging its telehealth provision, which has largely been responsible for preserving nationwide access to abortion since the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade in 2022. Louisiana filed the case on behalf of a woman who said her boyfriend had ordered abortion pills and forced her to take them.

In May, a federal appeals court granted Louisiana’s request to reinstate a nationwide requirement that mifepristone be dispensed in person. But the Supreme Court quickly blocked the decision while the case plays out.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. commissioned the safety review last year after a conservative think tank claimed to have found a higher rate of serious complications from mifepristone than the FDA reported. Several top Republicans, including Sen. Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, have also pressured the Trump administration to tighten access to the drug.

Researchers who study reproductive health said the think tank’s findings, which were neither peer-reviewed nor published in a medical journal, amounted to junk science. A wealth of data has shown that less than 0.5% of women who take mifepristone have serious adverse reactions.
It’s unclear what conclusion the FDA, which lacks a permanent commissioner, will draw from its new study.

President Donald Trump’s pick to lead the FDA, Dr. Heidi Overton, a White House adviser, is a fierce opponent of abortion rights, having previously described medication abortion as “dangerous to women.”
At her Senate confirmation hearing last month, Overton repeatedly sidestepped questions about mifepristone, including whether she believes the abortion pill is safe.

title: California woman accused of spying for China will be jailed while awaiting trial
summary: Wanying Zhang, a California woman accused of acting as a Chinese spy inside the U.S., will remain jailed pending her trial after a judge sided Wednesday with federal prosecutors who argued that she poses a flight risk.
story: LOS ANGELES — A California woman accused of acting as a Chinese spy inside the U.S. will remain jailed pending her trial after a judge sided Wednesday with federal prosecutors who argued that she poses a flight risk.

Wanying Zhang, 34, who sometimes goes by Heather, will remain in pretrial detention following the ruling by U.S. Magistrate Judge Steve Kim. The FBI arrested her Sunday at Los Angeles International Airport before she could board a flight to China.

In a criminal complaint, prosecutors accused Zhang of spying on a son of Taiwan’s president outside his residence in the Seattle area at the behest of Chinese officials. Zhang, of Irvine, about 42 miles southeast of downtown Los Angeles, hadn’t registered as a foreign agent as required, they said.

Zhang was represented in court Wednesday by veteran criminal defense attorney Craig Harbaugh, who argued she wouldn’t flee in part because of her strong family connections to Southern California, where she lives with her husband and two young daughters.

“The government’s theory — she’s been a sleeper agent for the last 10 years, working as a real estate agent, raising her family and will choose to go to China and abandon her work, her family and her home — it’s not supported,” Harbaugh said.

Zhang’s family had been willing to put up their home equity — valued at $700,000 — combined with bonds from her husband, his sister, his father and a family friend totaling $120,000 as an assurance that she would appear in court.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
But prosecutors countered that she had “hundreds of thousands of dollars available to her” in China, as well as investments in a business and contacts that could allow her to flee easily.

“I don’t think it’s a very strong argument that she’s that tied to her family here,” Assistant U.S. Attorney Amanda Elbogen said, casting Zhang as a lying foreign agent with the skills and resources to evade detection and capture.
An investigation found Zhang attended China’s University of International Relations, which an FBI investigator said in court documents is “closely affiliated with China’s intelligence apparatus.”

The charging document alleges Zhang had been communicating with a former classmate, who is now believed to be a Chinese official, through whom she had arranged an agreement to conduct surveillance of the Taiwanese president’s son. The document says she later captured photos, video and license plate information about him and sent them to her alleged Chinese handler.
She is alleged to have done all of that alongside an unidentified “Individual 1,” according to the complaint, who prosecutors said Wednesday had already fled to China two weeks ago.

Zhang wore a white jail jumpsuit and remained shackled for the entirety of Wednesday’s proceedings, a departure from her initial appearance Monday, when she was uncuffed and wore street clothes, with her hair neatly styled.

Wednesday’s hearing had several testy moments among prosecutors, Harbaugh and Kim, largely over whether Zhang’s pattern of one-way flights overseas was a credible defense that she wasn’t a flight risk and whether she had other U.S. properties to rely on for monetary assets.
Discussion in court revealed Zhang had disclosed only one residence to pretrial services, while her husband later revealed they owned two more, which her attorney said was a misunderstanding.
“She lied to pretrial services. She’s a real estate agent; she should know what properties she owns,” Elbogen countered.
Zhang is due back in court as early as Oct. 19 for a preliminary hearing — if federal prosecutors don’t indict her before then.

title: Trump wants to make his West Palm Beach golf club a permanent presidential retreat
summary: The proposed deal would also make Trump’s club the “permanent United States Presidential Golf Course,” which could be used “by all past, current and future” presidents, the club’s attorney said in a letter.
story: President Donald Trump wants to add a presidential retreat to his club in West Palm Beach, Florida, with his golf course there becoming the “permanent United States Presidential Golf Course.”

An attorney for the Trump International Golf Club proposed the designation and construction of a retreat on Trump’s dime in a letter to the Palm Beach County Board of County Commissioners, which has been obtained by NBC News.

“Just as Camp David, Windsor Palace or the Elysee Palace are known worldwide, so too will the Presidential Golf Course in Palm Beach County,” Harvey Oyer wrote in the letter last month, which was first reported by The Palm Beach Post.
The White House confirmed the proposal to The Washington Post on Wednesday. Trump, asked about the report in the Oval Office, told reporters that it had not been his idea but that he was on board.
“This was suggested to me by the military and Secret Service,” and it is “a great idea,” he said.
“They asked if I’d be willing to do it, and I said I would be,” he said.
“This wouldn’t be for me. This would be for all future presidents,” and it is “one of the best golf courses in the world,” Trump said.

Oyer’s letter asks the county, which owns the property the course is on, to give some of the land to the federal government for the project. The club would work with the government to design an “appropriate Presidential lodging facility” that the club would pay to construct.
A White House official said in a statement that the retreat could be used for presidents to “hold important meetings and utilize the amenities of a world-class property.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

“The property is minutes away from the Donald J. Trump International Airport, does not have buildings looming, does not have houses along the course, has great security features, is close to law enforcement, and happens to be a highly-rated golf course,” the statement said. “These are features that are necessary for any Presidential retreat.”

Trump, a frequent golfer who used to mock his predecessor Barack Obama during the 2016 presidential campaign for hitting the links, said Wednesday that “it seems all presidents play golf” and that the new retreat would be “used a lot.”
Oyer’s letter said the facility could be used by “all past, current and future U.S. presidents regardless of party affiliation and all visiting heads of state, regardless of party affiliation.”
A reporter for Fox News asked Trump whether the retreat would be called “Camp Donald.”
“It’s already called Trump International,” he replied.

title: The secret to a good night’s rest? Let sleeping dogs lie ... next to you
summary: A surprising new study found that people who sleep near their dogs don’t experience disrupted sleep. If anything we humans are the ones disturbing our dogs’ sleep.
story: There’s no feeling in the world like cuddling up at night with your pooch, even when we think they’re messing up our sleep by hogging space, stealing covers and yapping at random sounds.

A surprising new study found that people who sleep near their dogs don’t experience disrupted sleep. If anything, the University of Toronto researchers discovered, we humans are the ones disturbing our dogs’ sleep.

And we feel safer sleeping with our dogs, hinting at “a deeper evolutionary history” between humans and dogs, said study co-author Ming Fei Li, who was a graduate student of evolutionary anthropology during the research.

Activity trackers similar to Fitbits monitored the nighttime activity of 25 human volunteers and their 38 dogs in southern Ontario to monitor how each affected the other’s sleep. The study, which was published Wednesday in PLOS One, was conducted during the Covid pandemic as part of a larger project comparing the activity patterns of socialized wolves and domestic dogs.
For four weeks, the humans wore the devices on their wrists while the dogs, all huskies and malamutes with no health problems, wore them on their collars.
Most dogs slept on the bed or in the same room as their humans. A few dogs slept in different rooms, said anthropology researcher Lavania Nagendran, who was also a study author.
Using the activity trackers, they analyzed “objective sleep measures” of the people and their dogs, including sleep duration and sleep quality, Nagendran said.
The human volunteers also self-reported their sleep quality in an accompanying survey.

Though half of the people, particularly those who slept with more than one dog at a time, reported interrupted sleep, the activity tracker data found that sharing a bed with their dogs didn’t affect how well or how long the pups or their humans slept.

“When we looked at the subjective, or people’s perceived, sleep, we saw that there were people who reported poor sleep if they had multiple dogs,” Nagendran said. “But, again, that wasn’t seen in the devices.”

When they observed “synchronized activity states” with the devices, they found that humans and dogs became active around the same time while they were sleeping but that it was the humans who moved first and disturbed their dogs, not the other way around, Li said. That contradicts a 2020 study that found dogs influenced human movement more than humans influenced dog movement during the night.
The researchers also found it made no difference whether people’s dogs slept directly in the bed with them or in a nearby area.
There were limitations to the study, including the small group of volunteers, which consisted of more women than men, and a lack of variation in dog breeds, Li said.
For Subscribers
Previous research on co-sleeping with a dog has shown a link between poorer sleep and owning a pet and found that people sleep well with a dog nearby, but not in the bed.
For Subscribers

A 2023 study published in the journal Human-Animal Interactions found a link between pet ownership and poorer sleep, while a 2017 Mayo Clinic study found people slept better with a dog nearby except when the dog slept on the bed with them.
Dogs may actually improve our sleep habits by forcing us to adjust to consistent bedtime schedules — as anyone with a sleepy, whining dog can confirm.

Dogs are “zeitgebers”; that is, they provide cues about when it’s time to eat, take a walk or go to sleep, said W. Christopher Winter, a sleep medicine expert at Charlottesville Neurology & Sleep Medicine in Virginia.
“Dogs want things done on a certain rhythm, and that can be really positive for people who struggle with that,” Winter said.
Most sleep research shows that “creating internal consistency” around sleep habits may matter more than the amount of sleep a person gets, he said.
“It’s the consistent nature of sleep that is really important, and I think dogs do a wonderful job of creating that,” he said.
Not all dogs are good sleepmates, though.

A large dog, for example, may take up a lot of bed space and “hog the sheets,” while dogs of any size can wake during the night when they hear random sounds or see flashes of light, said Winter, who wasn’t involved in the study.
Some dogs, particularly dogs with upper airway abnormalities like pugs, Boston terriers and French bulldogs, may snore loudly, which could disturb their human companions, he said.
“Some of the worst snoring and sleep apnea I’ve ever heard has been a dog at 4 o’clock in the afternoon sleeping when you’re watching a football game,” Winter joked.

title: USS Lincoln nearly home after more than 300 days at sea
summary: Issues were raised about supplies and morale on board during the extended deployment. Navy documents showed eight service members attempted suicide.
story: ABOARD THE USS LINCOLN IN THE PACIFIC OCEAN — After spending more than 300 days at sea, service members aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln will finally return home this week.
The beleaguered aircraft carrier with about 7,500 personnel is scheduled to dock Thursday in San Diego, amid sharp criticism over its prolonged deployment in the Middle East.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth acknowledged to crewmembers on Wednesday that he was the “only thing standing between you and home” and that he had been the one “who signed that orders book twice” to extend the ship’s deployment.

On Wednesday, the evening before they were set to dock, the mood seemed far more jovial aboard the ship; sailors were chatting and laughing, some were running a 5K around a deck now free of aircraft. A band played in the setting sun.
Navy reports eight suicide attempts on USS Lincoln

The Lincoln left San Diego in November and was initially expected to return before the summer months. Its deployment was extended after the Iran war began in February. The ship was at sea without a port of call for 286 days until early September, when it docked in Thailand for a handful of days. By that point, family members of those on board had raised concerns about dwindling food supplies and low morale.

At least eight service members attempted suicide during the many months at sea, according to a letter sent last month to Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y., by a top Navy official. The letter, obtained by NBC News, prompted concerns about the impact to mental health that such a lengthy deployment can have on service members. No deaths on the ship have been attributed to suicide.

Some family members of those on the ship said the extended time at sea was “wreaking havoc” on sailors’ mental health, and one described it as a “scene out of the ‘American Horror Story’” television show.

“Where he had been very positive, he started getting very dark,” one woman told NBC News about her son’s time at sea. Another parent said that she and her daughter, who is serving aboard the ship, grew increasingly frustrated as the Trump administration continued to push back the ship’s arrival date.

According to U.S. officials, a sailor assigned to the air wing on the Lincoln went overboard in early August and was quickly rescued and treated. That sailor was transferred off the ship for further medical care, the official told NBC News.
Navy officials initially said leadership had not observed an increase in suicidal ideations or attempts aboard the ship.

According to the letter, suicide attempts occurred among crewmembers and sailors from the carrier air wing, strike group and destroyer squadron staff, escorting destroyers and all embarked aviation squadrons.

title: DNC sues administration over taxpayer-funded pro-Trump TV ads
summary: Trump announced this week that he and his PAC, MAGA Inc., would pay for the ads moving forward following bipartisan criticism.
story: The Democratic National Committee sued the Trump administration Wednesday over its taxpayer-funded advertisements that portray President Donald Trump in a favorable light, alleging the ads violate federal laws on government spending and propaganda.

The DNC cited a measure Trump signed into law this year that says funds appropriated by Congress can’t be used “for publicity or propaganda purposes within the United States not heretofore authorized by Congress.”

The lawsuit also cites the Anti-Deficiency Act, which bars spending government money that hasn’t been appropriated by Congress, and the Purpose Statute, which says taxpayer funds can be used only for the specific purposes approved by Congress.

The DNC said the administration’s use of taxpayer dollars for “campaign-style advertisements” deprived Democrats “of a fair electoral process by adding public funds to the resources available to support Republican candidates.” The use of public funds places Democratic candidates at an electoral disadvantage, it argued.
The watchdog group Common Cause filed its own suit making similar legal arguments, alleging the administration had violated appropriations statutes.
The ads, launched last month, sparked criticism from lawmakers on both sides of the aisle, many of whom questioned their legality.

Trump reversed course Monday, announcing on Truth Social he would no longer use government funds for the ads and saying he and his PAC, MAGA Inc., would foot the bill moving forward, instead. He didn’t say whether the government would be reimbursed for the ads that already ran.
For Subscribers

Reached for comment on the lawsuits, the White House pointed NBC News to Trump’s Truth Social post. The Department of Homeland Security and the Office of Management and Budget, which are named as defendants in addition to Trump and the White House, didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment on the lawsuit.
Since Trump’s announcement, several of the ads have continued to run with the disclaimer that they were paid for by the U.S. government.
Asked by NBC News whether those were paid for before or after Trump pledged to cover the costs, the White House wouldn’t say either way.

A person familiar with the ads said that the ad buy for the spots, placed before Trump’s Monday announcement, will end this week. Afterwards, the person said, outside groups will begin paying for the ads.
For Subscribers

NBC News has reported that a $20 million contract was awarded to a Maryland firm for the ad campaign. AdImpact, a political ad-tracking firm, estimated that at least $10 million had been spent to air the ads through Monday.

Attorneys for the DNC asked a federal judge in Washington to find that the administration acted unlawfully “by developing and airing the propaganda ads using Congressionally appropriated funds” and to prevent it from using those funds to develop and air the ads in the future.
DNC Chair Ken Martin condemned the administration for using taxpayer dollars as Americans struggle with a rising cost of living.
“Americans deserve better than to have their hard-earned tax dollars used for Trump’s illegal schemes,” he said in a statement Wednesday.

Omar Noureldin, Common Cause’s senior vice president of policy and litigation, said in an interview with NBC News Wednesday that the group is bringing forth the suit “because we want to make sure that no president, regardless of party, can hijack public funds to fund political self-promotion without congressional approval.”

“It appears that the $20 million that had been contracted for this has not all been spent yet, and so they will continue to run ads paid for by taxpayer dollars, and so we think we need to stop that now, and not another dollar of taxpayer dollars should be spent on these ads,” Noureldin said.
The federal money for the ads came from funds intended for Customs and Border Protection, an arm of DHS. NBC News reported that CBP leadership was cut out of the decision to run the ads.
Federal Communications Commission Chair Brendan Carr, a Trump appointee, said last week that the ads didn’t merit FCC review, arguing that they weren’t “anything at all out of the ordinary.”

The White House has defended the ads by calling them “clearly not political” and claiming they were about “reminding Americans to love their country.” It has also pointed to other administrations’ use of public safety announcements.

title: Appeals judges don’t reveal how they’ll rule on Saudi Arabia’s effort to end 9/11 litigation
summary: In lawsuits, hundreds of victims’ relatives and injured survivors claim that employees of the Saudi government assisted the hijackers.
story: Relatives of victims of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks packed a federal appeals courtroom in New York City on Wednesday as three judges heard arguments over whether legal claims against Saudi Arabia can proceed.
The judges revealed through their questions that there are still many legal issues to be decided in the lawsuit even though it has dragged on for almost a quarter-century.

They didn’t say when they might rule on whether claims can proceed to trial alleging that Saudi Arabia provided aid to at least two of the 19 men who hijacked planes and crashed them into the World Trade Center, the Pentagon and a Pennsylvania field that day.
Still, Terry Strada, whose husband, Tom Strada, was killed in the attacks, said she was encouraged that more than 100 family members of 9/11 victims turned out and by the judges’ questions.

“It really was a good day for us,” she said afterward. “The judges asked really meaningful questions and hammered the Saudi attorneys and didn’t let up. They weren’t buying what the Saudis were selling.”

Strada garnered attention during the 25th anniversary ceremony in New York last month when she implored President Donald Trump and Vice President Vance, who was in attendance, to seek answers from the Saudi government.
Outside the courthouse, Strada said she had not heard from the administration.
“Are you going to stand with the families?” she said. “Be the first president that ever would?”
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

In lawsuits, hundreds of victims’ relatives and injured survivors, along with insurance companies and businesses, claim that employees of the Saudi government directly and knowingly assisted the hijackers and other plotters and fueled Al Qaeda’s development into a terrorist organization by funding charities that supported them.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Some defendants, including Iran, the Taliban and Al Qaeda, already have been found in default.

On Wednesday, lawyers from both sides were questioned repeatedly by the appeals judges who seemed unsure exactly how they would respond to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia’s claims that it should be dismissed as a defendant on sovereign immunity grounds.
Lawyers for Saudi Arabia say the nation and the U.S. were partners in the 1990s against terrorism, Al Qaeda and its founder, Osama bin Laden.
Although 15 of the 19 attackers on 9/11 were Saudis, the Saudi government has long denied any involvement in the attacks.
Lawyers for victims’ relatives claim that a group of extremist religious leaders in Saudi Arabia aided the hijackers.

The appeal by Saudi Arabia stemmed from an August 2025 ruling by U.S. District Judge George B. Daniels, who decided that the case could proceed in federal court, though he did not rule on the merits of the claims.

October Prime Day ends at 11:59 p.m. PT on October 7 —  that’s October 8 at 2:59 a.m. ET, 1:59 a.m. CT and 12:59 a.m. MT.

Yes, October Prime Day is actually worth it, so long as you shop strategically. The sale offers some of the lowest prices of the year on products across categories, giving you a chance to start shopping for holiday gifts, upgrade outdated or broken items and restock your favorite basics, like skin care, cleaning supplies and groceries. Dawn Platinum Powerwash Dish Spray Bundle

This dish soap spray not only gets rid of grease and grime on your dishes, but it’s also gentle enough to clean surfaces like countertops and sinks, according to the brand. The value bundle comes with a spray bottle and three dish soap refills.
Lumineux Teeth Whitening Strips

These Lumineux whitening strips are one of our favorite at-home whitening treatments. They’re not made with peroxides that can irritate sensitive gums. The gel formula helps remove yellow plaque and break up stains on teeth, according to the brand. You apply the strips once daily for 30 minutes for seven consecutive days. This pack comes with 21 treatments, which is a three-month supply.
Medicube Collagen Jelly Cream

After reviewing Medicube for months, our NBC Selected editors determined it’s actually worth the hype. Right now, Amazon is discounting a ton of the brand’s bestselling products, including the Booster Pro X2, Deep Vitamin C Capsule Cream, Salmon PDRN Pink Collagen Jelly Gel Mask and Collagen Night Wrapping Mask. This cream has a light, jelly-like texture and has a pink tint at first, but dries down to a transparent finish after you apply it.
Listerine Alcohol Free Mouthwash Packets (30 Pack)

Keep your breath fresh while on the go with these mouthwash packets. I love taking these with me on trips because they’re slim, lightweight and fit in any bag or purse.  Each packet has the perfect amount of mouthwash for a full swish, too.
Amazon Smart Plug

The Amazon Smart Plug lets you control devices like lamps, fans and small kitchen appliances directly on an app or via voice commands. You can set timers, schedules and routines on the app, and the plug is compact enough to keep your second outlet free.
Scrub Daddy Scrub Mommy Kitchen Sponges

The Scrub Mommy sponges are a staple in my house. I love that they’re dual-sided: the textured side scrubs off any food and grime on my dishes, while the sponge side is soft enough to finish off the cleaning process. Plus, the sponge’s signature smiley face lets you get a secure grip and wipe down utensils. The Scrub Mommy is odor-resistant, scratch-free and dishwasher-safe.
Nodpod Gentle Pressure Sleep Mask
This weighted sleep mask provides gentle pressure that’ll help you fall asleep faster, according to the brand. It’s made from breathable jersey cotton on one side and plush microfleece on the other.
Vital Proteins Collagen Peptides Powder

Mix this collagen powder into either hot and cold beverages, including water, smoothies, coffee and tea. It has collagen sourced from grass-fed, pasture-raised bovine, vitamin C and hyaluronic acid to keep bones, joints, nails and hair healthy, according to the brand.
Reacher Sound Machine Sunrise Alarm Clock

Make mornings a little more peaceful with this sunrise alarm clock, which also serves as a sound machine and nightlight. They can choose from 26 sleep sounds, including white noise and rain, and set both the sound and night light on a timer for up to 180 minutes. For a smooth wake-up, they can also adjust the sunrise duration and pair it with one of eight alarm sounds (or none).
Waterpik Aquarius Water Flosser

This ADA-accepted water flosser has 10 pressure settings and a 22-ounce, dishwasher-safe water reservoir. You can use one of the seven included tips to clean different areas of your teeth, according to the brand. The water flosser also has a one-minute timer with a 30-second pacer to help you brush the expert-recommended two minutes.
FYY Travel Cable Organizer Pouch

Organize your charging cables, cords, portable chargers and more with this compact pouch. It has two layers of storage space to hold all your devices and chargers in one place. It’s also water-resistant to give you peace of mind while you travel.
Laneige Lip Sleeping Mask

This lip mask is a tried and true NBC Select editor favorite and leaves lips hydrated and glossy. It comes in a range of scents and includes a tiny spatula, so you don’t have to use your fingers to apply it.
Lysol Disinfecting Wipes Bundle (4-Pack)

This bundle comes with four packs of Lysol Disinfectant Wipes, each of which have 80 wipes (320 total). Use these to wipe messes and disinfect bathrooms, classrooms, seats on public transportation and more. Packs come in three different scents: lemon lime, mango hibiscus and crisp linen.
Energizer AA and AAA Batteries (48 Count)

If you’re stocking up on household essentials this October Prime Day, consider this pack of 48 AA and AAA Energizer batteries (24 each). They can last up to 10 years in storage (which means you don’t have to worry about using them right away).
Core Power Fairlife Protein Milk Shakes

Take these ready-to-drink protein shakes to the gym, work or anywhere else you’ll need a morning or afternoon snack. Each shake has 26 grams of protein and is lactose-free. You can buy this pack of 12 in three flavors, including chocolate, strawberry banana and vanilla (all of which are currently on sale).
La Roche-Posay Toleriane Hydrating Gentle Facial Cleanser

This fragrance-free cleanser is excellent for dry, sensitive skin. It has glycerin, ceramides and niacinamide to repair and maintain the skin’s natural moisture barrier. Plus, the pump applicator makes it easy to use and mess-free.
Hero Cosmetics Original Mighty Patch (75 Count)

These expert-recommended pimple patches help heal breakouts using hydrocolloid, a fluid-absorbing gel that draws out gunk, sebum and debris from your pimples, according to the brand. The patch has a translucent matte finish that blends into your skin tone.
Cascade Platinum Dishwasher Pods (59 Count)
Stock up on dishwasher tablets this fall Prime Day with this 59-pack from Cascade. The pods soak, scrub and rinse dishes while leaving behind a fresh, clean scent.
Salt & Stone Body Wash

This is my favorite body wash and I’ve gotten most of my friends and family hooked on it, too. It lathers nicely, moisturizes my skin and smells great. Plus, the bergamot and hinoki scent actually lasts on my skin. It comes in four more scents, all of which are on sale for Prime Day.
Ring Battery Doorbell 2K

Ring’s doorbell camera lets you monitor your space using your phone, tablet or computer and get real-time notifications. The Wi-Fi-equipped camera pairs with the companion Ring app, so you can see, hear and speak to visitors. It works with Amazon Alexa voice assistant, too.
Olaplex Wash & Shine Hair Kit

This Olaplex set comes with full sizes of the No.4 Bond Maintenance Shampoo, the No.5 Bond Maintenance Conditioner and the No.7 Bonding Oil to hydrate, detangle and protect your hair from heat, according to the brand. Each product is suitable for all hair types.
Casper Sleep Original Pillow

I have multiple Casper pillows I use every night; they’re incredibly soft, breathable and durable (they’ve lasted me multiple years without any snags or rips). I also love that they keep their shape, so I don’t have to worry about constantly fluffing them. This pillow has a medium-soft feel, which helps keep your head and neck aligned in any sleep position, according to the brand.
Ecolution Micro-Pop

This kitchen gadget lets you make fresh popcorn at home  It has a built-in measuring cup on the lid for kernels, so you can pour them into the popper and microwave it for about three minutes. The top also has holes that melt butter onto the popcorn.
Paula's Choice Skin Perfecting 2% BHA Liquid Exfoliant

This toner is one of our favorite liquid exfoliants because it helps unclog pores and smooth fine lines, according to the brand. “I can actually notice a difference in the size of my pores after using this product a few times,” says NBC Selected commerce editor Cory Fernandez. “It also doesn’t sting or irritate my seborrheic dermatitis at all, which is always a plus.”
Dae Cactus Fruit 3-in-1 Styling Cream & Taming Wand

This Dae taming wand is a favorite among our editors, who say it keeps frizz, flyaways and baby hairs at bay for hours. I use it every time to keep flyaways down when my hair is in a bun or ponytail. The tube has Dae’s viral styling cream (which is also on sale) inside, and it never makes my hair look or feel crunchy.
COSRX Snail Mucin 96% Repairing Serum

According to experts in our guide to snail mucin, the buzzy ingredient hydrates and plumps skin while also targeting fine lines. This Cosrx serum, one of our favorite facial essences, is lightweight and hypoallergenic, meaning it’s safe for sensitive skin, according to the brand.
Tide Odor + Oxi Laundry Detergent Pods 63-pack

The detergent inside each of these Tide Pods helps clean, fight odors, remove stains, protect colors and keep your clothes smelling fresh, according to the brand. You get 63 Tide Pods in this pack, which come in a resealable container.
AncestryDNA DNA Test Kit

AncestryDNA analyzes your DNA to trace your origins and ethnicities and find your distant relatives by scanning over 3,600 regions worldwide. The process includes sending a saliva sample in the included prepaid package to the AncestryDNA lab, and you’ll get your results online in six to eight weeks, according to the service.
Tower 28 SunnyDays SPF 30 Tinted Sunscreen

Tower 28’s tinted SPF is a favorite among NBC Selected editors, including myself. It has enough coverage to even out my skin tone and cover up my redness, so I can use the sunscreen in lieu of foundation. It has the National Eczema Association’s Seal of Acceptance, which means it’s safe for sensitive skin, plus it’s fragrance-free, alcohol-free and noncomedogenic.
Spot & Tango PupGum Dog Dental Chews

My 8-year-old dog Havanese and bichon frise mix, Bella, loves these Pupgum dental chews from Spot & Tango, which are currently at their lowest price ever. Each pack comes with 28 chews that help  scrape away build up on your dog’s teeth and freshen their breath. You can choose from three sizes: small (for dogs up to 15 pounds), medium (up to 40 pounds) and large (41 pounds or more).
Clean Skin Club Clean Towels XL (2-Pack)

I’m very careful about using face towels because they can harbor bacteria quickly. I started using these disposable towels to dry my face after washing it, and it’s become a staple in my daily routine. Since I go through them quickly, I jump on any opportunity to get them on sale (especially if it comes in a multipack).
Sol de Janeiro Brazilian Bum Bum Cream

Sol de Janeiro’s body creams have some of my favorite scents, and they make my skin feel soft and hydrated. This classic Cheirosa 62 scent has notes of pistachio, salted caramel and vanilla. Plus, the cream has caffeine and coconut oil to tighten and soften skin, according to the brand.
Amazon Fire TV Stick HD

You can plug in Amazon’s Fire Stick into an HDMI port to stream entertainment from your favorite platforms and watch live TV in HD. The Fire Stick comes with a remote that lets you control the TV via buttons or voice commands.

These compostable, plant-based wipes are fragrance-free and have the National Eczema Association’s seal of acceptance, so they’re safe to use on babies and those with sensitive skin, according to the brand. This set comes with 10 packs, which has 72 wipes each (a total of 720 wipes).
Hefty Ultra Strong 13-Gallon Trash Bags

These stretchy, multilayered trash bags are made to avoid rips and therefore prevent leaks. They have a drawstring to keep everything inside once they’re full and each bag has baking soda and added fragrance to neutralize odors, too.
Healthy Packers Ice Packs

Keep food cold with these slim, flat, reusable ice packs. They come in a pack of four and stay cold for hours, according to the brand. Fill them with water once and freeze them overnight before using them.
CeraVe Moisturizing Cream

This Cerave cream earned a top 10 spot in our list of 100 best moisturizers. It’s gentle, fragrance-free and has the National Eczema Association Seal of Acceptance, so it’s a great option for those with very sensitive skin. It has a thick texture, but it absorbs quickly into the skin, leaving no residue or a heavy, uncomfortable feeling, according to our editors.
Revlon One-Step Volumizer Plus

A slimmer and sleeker version of the original Revlon One-Step Hair Dryer, this hot tool comes with a detachable head that makes it travel- and storage-friendly. It has four heat settings and a ceramic titanium barrel to get a fresh blowout at home.

title: Valerie Bertinelli Defends Tribute To Eddie Van Halen: ‘I Love Ed. Never Stopped Loving Ed’
summary: Actor Valerie Bertinelli is defending herself against online haters who criticized her recent tribute to her late ex-husband, Eddie Van Halen.
story: Actor Valerie Bertinelli is defending herself against online haters who criticized her recent tribute to her late ex-husband, Eddie Van Halen.

Bertinelli doubled down on her recent Instagram post in honor of the sixth anniversary of the rock icon’s death Oct. 6. The tribute post prompted some fans to accuse her of holding on to the old relationship. But in a new video shared Oct. 7, Bertinelli told her critics that “you can’t bother me.”
“I love Ed. Never stopped loving Ed. And my heart loves a lot,” she said in the clip. “Don’t you wish yours could too?”
Bertinelli’s throwback photo featured the one-time couple, sharing a laugh in a car.
“Photos may fade, like old photos do, but not the memories and never the love,” the 66-year-old wrote in the post’s caption.

The former “One Day at a Time” and “Hot in Cleveland” star was married to Van Halen from 1981 until 2007. She filed for divorce in 2005 after being separated for several years. The musician went on to marry Janie Liszewski in 2009, with whom he remained married until his death. Meanwhile, Bertinelli married financial planner Tom Vitale in 2011. They divorced in 2022.

Bertinelli, who shares a son with the rocker, musician Wolfgang Van Halen, 35, hit back at the criticisms in the new video that was captioned, “Strap in haters, let’s go for a little ride.” She told fans that she gets “pushback” any time she posts about her late ex.

Bertinelli, who remained close with Eddie Van Halen after their divorce — and was at the rocker’s bedside when he died in 2020 after a 20-year battle with cancer—  said often critics tell her she’s “not allowed to love” her former husband.
Those critics, she said, “berate you and berate you for months, make you think you’re crazy, until you finally say, ‘OK, fine, I don’t love him.’”
The scorn has caused her to remove images of  the late music legend from her account, Bertinelli said.

“They will never say, ‘Take that picture down, the one of your ex-husband along with you and your son in better days,’” she shared. “But they say that you’re obsessed, say all kinds of f----- up s--- until you take the picture down,” she said.
Bertinelli revealed that the musician, whom she began dating when she was 20, still holds a “big piece” of her heart.

“If I ever fall in love again, I’ll make room in my heart for that person, without it touching the love I have for Ed, my son, my daughter-in-law, all the people that I love,” she said. “Your heart opens up. Because your heart can hold a lot of love. All of our hearts can.”

title: Her Home Burned. Her Late Husband’s Basketball Hoop Didn’t. Now She’s Building Again
summary: Layla Hawkins is one of the thousands who were displaced by the Pacific Palisades fire that swept through the Los Angeles neighborhood, destroying some 6,800 homes, businesses and structures in one of the largest and most expensive disasters in California history.
story: Layla Hawkins had less than 10 minutes to pack up her cherished belongings before a wildfire on Jan. 7, 2025 took her beloved home of four decades. It left behind only a treasured basketball hoop that belonged to her late husband, Los Angeles sports star Tommy Hawkins, a motivation for the grieving homeowner to rebuild again in his honor.

Layla Hawkins is one of the thousands who were displaced by the Pacific Palisades fire that swept through the Los Angeles neighborhood, destroying some 6,800 homes, businesses and structures in one of the largest and most expensive disasters in California history. The blaze left 12 people dead.

Now, almost two years after the fires, Layla Hawkins is on the road to fulfilling her goal in memory of her late husband, thanks in part to nonprofit Habitat for Humanity, whose volunteers from its ReBUILD LA initiative are helping her pick up the pieces. She tells TODAY.com that she is “forever grateful.”
Hawkins says that seeing people come together to help her is “like having an army of relatives surrounding you and giving you hope, love and generous hugs. That’s priceless.”

The Palisades fire — in addition to the Eaton fire that burned simultaneously on the opposite end of Los Angeles, claiming the lives of 19 people and destroying 9,418 homes and other buildings — was an eye-opening experience for Hawkins. That day, she left her home with her husband’s ashes in hand and dog Shiloh. She says she could feel the heat from the fire.

“I lived in Malibu for 40 years. I had gone through quite a few fires and we have always been ready to go and get everything ready and come back,” Hawkins says. “That day, it was something out of a movie script. We only had about eight minutes to vacate and leave.”
She said she hoped evacuating would be similar to her past experiences in which she’d eventually return to see her home still standing. She wasn’t so lucky.

“I could see the fires viciously going crazy, way out of control. And I said to myself, and I said to my home, ‘I will see you in a few hours, like all the other times. Don’t worry, we’ll be fine,’” she recalls. “And as I stopped for just some reason, out of the blue, I looked back. I (had) a lump in my throat and I just knew that I would never see my home again.”
When she arrived back on her property later on, she hesitated before stepping out of her car, she recalls. Little remained of her home, she says.
However, a moment of optimism filled her heavy heart after she saw a blue starfish bank where she and her husband would share love notes with each other, she adds.
“I looked in that massive destruction, and I saw that little starfish, blue, deep blue, just staring at me,” she says. “I just went over there, and I remember I kneeled, and I said, ‘Tommy.’”

Even more moving, Hawkins says, was the discovery that her husband’s basketball hoop had survived the fire. Tommy Hawkins had a 10-year NBA career and played for the Los Angeles Lakers for six seasons, as well as with the Cincinnati Royals for four. He also worked with the Los Angeles Dodgers as vice president of communications.
“I remember I walked over and I gave it a big hug,” she says. “I hugged it so tight because I was hugging my home. I was hugging Tommy.”
From that moment, she made a promise to her late husband that she would return and rebuild their home.

Rebuilding efforts have been difficult, she says, but she made inroads on that promise after she received an email from Habitat for Humanity, informing her that they would help her reconstruct. She was shocked, she says, and read the email over and over to make sure it was real.

“It took me a few hours to actually settle down and write a letter to them. And from that day on, they have been with me every step,” she says, adding that they’ve helped with paperwork, permits and more.

Most recently, Habitat for Humanity of Greater Los Angeles held a four-day Pacific Palisades Community Build effort, from Sept. 23–26, during which Hawkins saw hundreds of volunteers working on her home as well as that of others. The group’s wall-framing and landscaping efforts, she says, brought a sense of community back to the destroyed land.
“I just (have) this feeling that I’m going to have the biggest Christmas tree up in my home by Christmastime,” she says with a laugh, adding that Habitat’s help has made her smile once again.
The expected completion date for Hawkins’ home is June 2027, pending weather.

title: Jeremy Allen White Reveals If He’d Want to Play Gene Wilder In Upcoming Biopic
summary: Jeremy Allen White has often drawn comparisons to the legendary Gene Wilder. He answers if he’d want to play the actor in a biopic.
story: Between his magnetic screen presence and curly blond hair, Jeremy Allen White has often drawn comparisons to the legendary Gene Wilder.

“The Bear” star does not shy away from it, even if it means potentially accepting the intimidating task of playing the iconic “Young Frankenstein” and “Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory” actor onscreen.

A biopic of Wilder is in the works, but there has been no announcement yet of who will play him, according to Deadline. White, 35, was asked by Craig Melvin on TODAY Oct. 7 if he would be interested in the role.

“Absolutely, it would be my honor,” White said. “‘Young Frankenstein’ is one of my earliest film memories. ‘Blazing Saddles’ — he was a genius, it would be an honor. I love him, I’ve always loved him. I need the call.”
White so strikingly resembles a young Wilder that it’s become a meme online. He noted in a 2024 interview with Buzzfeed that the two have no relation.
“I’m not related to Gene Wilder,” White said. “I think a lot of people think I am.”
Director Dito Montiel and writer Jeremy Roth are set to create the  Wilder biopic, Deadline reported in June. Wilder died at 83 in 2016.

White revealing that he would welcome the role came after his reflections on the weight that comes with portraying real-life figures. He played a young Bruce Springsteen in the 2025 film “Deliver Me From Nowhere.”
“It was a wonderful experience, but it was a tremendous amount of pressure,” White said on TODAY about playing The Boss.
The actor admittedly had “a little hesitation” about his latest role in “The Social Reckoning” because he’s playing another real person. He stars as former Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz.

“I think I was just anxious about the idea of going ahead and playing another real person right away and feeling that responsibility again,” he said. “I think I wanted my next thing to be something that was just my own and my own kind of creation and to feel no pressure to do any kind of impersonation.”
But it was “The Social Reckoning” director Aaron Sorkin who put White at ease.

“Learn as much as you can, read his book, watch interviews, but don’t feel like you have to do any kind of mimicry,” White recalled of Sorkin’s guidance. “Make it your own. So it was kind of the best of both worlds.”

title: ‘Heated Rivalry’ Annotated Scripts Reveal How Shane and Ilya’s First Meeting Was Actually Supposed to Happen
summary: The pivotal first scene of “Heated Rivalry,” in which hockey stars Shane and Ilya meet for the very first time, was written and filmed to be way longer than what viewers saw in the final cut.
story: It is a truth universally acknowledged that a good story starts with a good first line. In TODAY’s “Cold Open,” authors tease their buzzy upcoming release by revealing and explaining its first line, paragraph or page.

The pivotal first scene of the TV adaptation of “Heated Rivalry,” in which hockey stars Shane and Ilya meet for the very first time, was written and filmed to be way longer than what viewers saw in the final cut.

TODAY.com has an exclusive first look at “I’ll Believe in Anything,” a book about the making of Season 1 of “Heated Rivalry,” featuring scripts annotated by the show’s creator, writer and director, Jacob Tierney.

In an excerpt of the script, Tierney reveals that the first scene of the show — about a minute long in the episode’s final cut — was originally written to be up to six minutes. It sees a teenage Shane Hollander, played by Hudson Williams, introduce himself to another junior hockey prodigy, Ilya Rozanov, played by Connor Storrie, at a junior hockey tournament in Regina, Saskatchewan.
Fans of the show know that their meeting sets in motion a yearslong secret romantic tryst, occurring in the background of their respective rises through the ranks of professional hockey.

The scene starts with Shane awkwardly approaching Ilya outside a rink while the latter smokes a cigarette. In the final cut of Episode 1, they only exchange a few words. The two shake hands, Shane comments on the “no smoking” sign above Ilya’s head before calling the Russian “an awesome player to watch.” The teens taunt each other briefly before Shane heads inside.
But the annotated script reveals that their first conversation was much more substantial, with plenty of teasing.

“This was shot exactly as scripted, and then we cut it down,” Tierney writes. “Our editor Arthur Tarnowski would present an option of what a scene looks like at a minute and a half, or three minutes, six minutes, or whatever it was.”
The cut dialogue begins with Shane asking Ilya if his parents are at the tournament. After he answers no, Shane says, “That must suck. With Christmas and all.”
“Christmas is later in Russia,” Ilya says.
Awkward silence continues to ensure, and Shane finally breaks it by commenting on how next year’s event will occur in his hometown of Ottawa, Canada.
“Is Ottawa more exciting?” Ilya responds, after the stage directions note he “can’t help but smirk a bit at Shane’s nerves.”
After “they both kind of smile at each other,” Ilya makes the next remark, asking if Shane’s parents are with him.
“Yeah, they try to come to most of my games,” Shane says.
“Nice for you,” Ilya responds.
Tierney also describes his goal for how he wanted Shane and Ilya to come across to viewers in this first scene. He writes he wanted to show a “charming formality to Shane.”
“He’s trying to be a good sport and wants to introduce himself, and he has a bit of awkward-dad energy,” Tierney writes in the annotations.
Of Ilya, he adds, “I wanted people to watch Ilya go from suspicious to quite playful, to show that playfulness would come. It would be a hallmark of his personality.”

title: Our 1 Question for Magnus Ferrell At Commercial: Where Did Will Ferrell’s Son Get His ‘Funky White Boy’ Sound?
summary: Magnus Ferrell talks about his dad, Will Ferrell, the success of his song “Asleep Talking” and what’s next.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on air.
Magnus Ferrell is having a breakout moment, with a little help from his enthusiastic dad, Will Ferrell.
Earlier this year, Will Ferrell played a snippet of Magnus Ferrell’s song “Asleep Talking” during an appearance on Michelle Obama and her brother Craig Robinson’s podcast.
Their instantly genuine reactions led to a viral moment and a spotlight on the 22-year-old’s music, which he’s been making for years.

Magnus Ferrell, a sensitive, soulful crooner known for his falsetto voice and funky beat, may seem like a contrast to his father, whose voice has been famously likened to a “combination of Fergie and Jesus.”
But jazz musicianship is actually all in the family. Will Ferrell’s father, Roy Lee Ferrell, toured with the Righteous Brothers for 20 years.
We caught up with Magnus Ferrell after his appearance on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle on Sept. 30, where he also performed his breakout hit.

I had known known beforehand that was happening. I just knew that he was going to play the song. I was in Oregon at the time, and I had forgot that it was happening because the podcast interview (was taped) three or four weeks before. I’m in the middle of the woods with no cell service, and the only connection to the internet was the Wi-Fi in the cabin. I just kept running back and forth to the cabin into the woods, trying to be present where I was, but also trying to check in on this moment and my life dreams happening before my eyes, which was unbelievable.

I was kind of jaded to it because I’ve like been so lucky to have that my whole life. It was kind of a moment of like, oh my gosh, people don’t know him as a dad. They know him as the actor, and and we’ve kept the family side of things super private. It was just cool for everyone to see that moment and how he is as my dad. It meant a lot to me because that was his pure reaction. I’m just so lucky to have that support.
Yeah. I just never thought ever that my music would connect with that many people, but here we are.

I’ve been playing piano since I was 5 years old, and music has just kind of been a part of our family for a very long time. My dad’s dad, my grandpa, was a touring musician and toured with the Righteous Brothers. He played keys, piano, organ and alto sax.

Exactly, that’s where the groove comes from. This whole experience has made me just reflect on the past. There’s so many emotions of like, “S---, am I ready for this? Is this what I want to do? Is this like what I want my existence to be?”

I just think everything happens for a reason. I’ve been putting on music for five years now, so it’s been a while. I’ve had a lot of time to develop, which I’m very, very very thankful for. I’m really lucky that I wasn’t thrust into the spotlight when I put out my first song. I’m very sensitive, and I care a lot about my music. And I think if that had happened when I was younger and more green, it might have discouraged me from continuing.
One of the best things I’ve learned is not everybody’s going to like your music, so you have to really focus on making music for yourself that you can listen to.

I believe with the position that I’m in, I have this obvious advantage just in terms of spotlight. I’m the son of an actor. That’s going to be something that is just there. So I really pride myself on my work ethic and practicing my instruments, my vocals and my piano and all the other things I want to really get good at. I still think that there’s there’s a lot that I want to get better at, and I have a lot of potential to continue to improve. I’m not exactly where I want to be yet in terms of like my musicianship. I now feel really comfortable in the position I’m in. But yeah, I’m just excited to to just get better.

I grew up in jazz band and met one of my best friends and closest collaborators through jazz band. In terms of writing and putting out music together, that is something that I felt like was missing from the earlier music I was making. “Asleep Talking” was the first one that was like, “Oh, finally, this is what I’ve been searching for.” This is something that I would listen to on my own. I’m happy with how this sounds, and I’m not analyzing too much what’s going on. It’s not crafted too heavy.

I felt this way after an event and a certain experience that happened. We wrote about it. We tried to take the feeling of that event and put it into the song, and every part of it, I’m happy with. There’s not a thing that I’m like, “Oh, I wish we could have changed that. Oh, I wish this melody was different.” All of it, I’m happy with and satisfied.

It’s a really high honor, and I still got a lot to prove, you know. Just that world of like the funky white boy, like Justin Timberlake. It’s a lot to live up to, but I’m excited to do so and to take it as a challenge and an opportunity to show the world what my sound is and and just continue to make music that I love.
It was funny for sure. For the most part, I don’t get surprised by his antics, but that one caught me off guard.
The photo of me being looking like I’m mad is just the reaction, “Oh my god, you got me. I had no idea you were going to do this.” Normally I’m prepared but it completely caught me off guard

title: I’m a John Steinbeck Expert. This Is What I Really Think of Netflix’s ‘East of Eden’
summary: Two John Steinbeck experts unpack East of Eden and explain why they like the depiction of Cathy.
story: “Take it From Me” is a TODAY series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields.
Jeffrey Yeager sat down to watch the Netflix adaptation of the book he’s spent his career studying.

The vice president of the International Society of Steinbeck Scholars went into “East of Eden,” the seven-episode series directed and written by Zoë Kazan, with a “skeptical eye.” The show premiered just one day earlier, but he’d already heard chatter about how “it’s different than the book.”
Seven episodes later, he was won over by Kazan’s interpretation, which came over 60 years after her grandfather Elia Kazan directed the 1955 film adaptation.
“I came out very pleased. I thought it was fantastic,” Yeager tells TODAY.com.

“East of Eden” was the book Steinbeck considered his epic. At over 600 pages, the book is long enough to contain the origin stories of two sets of brothers, both loosely based on the Genesis story of Cain and Abel. The sprawling book, spanning the Civil War era to World War I, also maps out how two families came to live in California’s Salinas Valley: the Hamiltons and the Trasks.
Both the book and its characters are concerned with good and evil, free will and fate.
“Do our genes dictate who we are? Do our genes dictate the path we have in life, or do we have freedom in who we become?” Yeager summarizes the questions “East of Eden” asks.

Cal Trask (Joseph Zada in the show) is particularly consumed by these questions the more he finds out about his mother, Cathy Ames (Florence Pugh), and wonders if he’s destined to carry her less-than-golden legacy.
Steinbeck experts say Cathy’s nuanced depiction in Kazan’s “East of Eden” is what makes it so remarkable.

“I like the opening episode, and I like the fact that (Kazan) sets out the themes really clearly in terms of Cathy and the meditation on good and evil,” Susan Shillinglaw, a professor of English at San Jose State University who served as the university’s director of the Steinbeck Center for 18 years, tells TODAY.com.

In “East of Eden,” Steinbeck likens Cathy to a monster, writing in his introduction of the character, “The face and body may be perfect, but if a twisted gene or a malformed egg can produce physical monsters, may not the same process produce a malformed soul?”
According to Yeager, Cathy, in the book, is depicted as the “epitome of evil,” and “somebody who’s just missing something that is key to being human.”
Certainly, Cathy does evil things in both the TV show and book, including killing her own parents and attempting to kill the father of her twins (and that’s not all).
But Kazan says she set out to understand where Cathy’s monstrousness came from, reframing her childhood to include sexual assault.

Take the situation with her teacher as another example of how the show casts a different light on Cathy. In the book, she clearly manipulates a teacher to the point that he takes his own life. “But in the show, the teacher is trying to abuse her, and then she takes advantage of the situation,” Yeager says.
Rather than being wicked, Yeager says Pugh’s Cathy is “trying to redefine morality in her own way.”
Yeager applaudes Pugh’s performance, which shuffles between “reptilian eyes” and scenes that can draw empathy.

“I feel like the show can’t make its mind up on where it wants to go (with Cathy), and in some ways, that makes the show richer than the novel. It makes us think more about that character. How does evil come into the world?” Yeager says.
“The whole point of ‘East of Eden’ is to engage readers in an assessment of who Cathy is.”
For Shillinglaw, the show’s changing interpretations of Cathy are right in line with the legacy of the book.

“The whole point of ‘East of Eden’ is to engage readers in an assessment of who Cathy is,” Shillinglaw says. “She’s like the white whale in ‘Moby Dick.’ You have to keep looking at her. What does she mean? What is her purpose in the book?”
Yeager, after watching all seven episodes, wishes more attention had been given to the Hamiltons, the family Steinbeck based on his own.
“The Hamilton family was Steinbeck sort of tracing his lineage, and I can see why that wouldn’t be important for the story the show was trying to tell,” Yeager says.

He praises Hoon Lee’s “emotionally charged performance” as Lee, Aron and Cal Trask’s caretaker who plays an important role in healing the family at the end of the show. He’s also the voice of the story’s most overarching lesson: Timshel, a Hebrew word that’s translated to allow for free will in the triumph over evil, rather than fate.

For Shillinglaw, who taught a course on Steinbeck, says the conversations around “East of Eden” were always her favorite, and anticipates more brought on by the show, currently No. 1 on Netflix in the U.S.
“Students just found (the book) fascinating, and it was because of Cathy — what she meant and her legacy.”

title: ‘Days of Our Lives’ Star Robert Kelker-Kelly Dies at 62
summary: Longtime soap star Robert Kelker-Kelly, best known for portraying Bo Brady on “Days of Our Lives,” has died at age 62.
story: Longtime soap star Robert Kelker-Kelly, best known for portraying Bo Brady on “Days of Our Lives,” has died at age 62.
Kelly died on Oct. 3 in Missouri, according to a statement to NBC News by Kathleen Diebold Hargrave, the division director of the Office of the Regional Medical Examiner in St. Charles, Mo.
The cause of death is not available at this time, according to the statement. The timeline for death certification is normally 12 weeks, per the medical examiner’s office.
TMZ was first to report the news.
The Witchita, Kansas, native launched his daytime television career when he originated the role of Sam Fowler on “Another World” from 1987 until 1990.
He began playing rebel-turned-police detective Bo Brady on “Days of Our Lives” in 1992 after Peter Reckell, the actor who originated the role nearly a decade before, left the series.
Kelker-Kelly’s character was embroiled in a love triangle alongside Hope Brady, played by Kristian Alfonso, and Billie Reed, played by Lisa Rinna.

Rinna made headlines earlier this year when she detailed her challenging behind-the-scenes relationship with Kelker-Kelly in her memoir, “You Better Believe I’m Gonna Talk About It: A Candid New York Times Bestselling Memoir of Hollywood, Aging, and Owning It All.”
Kelker-Kelly left “Days of Our Lives” when Reckell resumed the role of Bo in 1995.
Kelker-Kelly returned to “Another World” from 1996 to 1998 to play professional race car driver Bobby Reno, who was later revealed to be Dr. Shane Roberts.
The actor next took on the role of Stavros Cassadine on “General Hospital,” appearing in more than 40 episodes from 2001 to 2014.
Kelker-Kelly won a Soap Opera Digest Award in 1994 for outstanding lead actor and another the following year for hottest soap couple, which he shared with Rinna.
Kelker-Kelly was married to fellow “Days of our Lives” star Miriam Parrish from 1997 until 2013, according to IMDB.

title: Anna Camp Is Nearly Unrecognizable on TODAY After Dramatic Hair Transformation
summary: Anna Camp traded in her blond hair for brown hair and showed off the new look in a TODAy appearance on October 6.
story: The blonde look that was Anna Camp’s signature in everything from “True Blood” to “Pitch Perfect” over more than 15 years has given way to her “brunette era.”

The actor had some fans doing a double take when she first revealed her new hair on Instagram in September. She also showed off the brunette look on TODAY Oct. 6 to promote her new HGTV show, “A Very Haunted Renovation.”
“The same but different.. brunette era loading now 🧉” Camp wrote on Instagram Sept. 7.
Fans were on board with the dramatic change from the blonde look she has worn as a vampire, snobby sorority sister, “Scream 7” horror queen and blonde twins on “You.”
“Beautiful! I mean you look good either way, blonde or brunette. 🤎” one fan commented.
“I mean… gorgeous either way! ❤️” another wrote.
“Looks great!” another commented.
One fan asked Camp what color her natural hair is.
“A little lighter than this!” she replied.
Camp, 44, still has the platinum blonde look on her new HGTV show, which features a renovation competition at one of America’s most haunted homes.
In keeping with the haunted theme, the actor will also be returning to the stage in a production of “2:22 A Ghost Story” at the Lucille Lortel Theatre in New York City in October.
“I like the spooky stuff and Halloween’s coming up, so it’s my season, I’m excited,” she said on TODAY.

title: Jenna Bush Hager Says Her October 2026 Book Club Pick Is By an Author on Her ‘Mt. Rushmore of Writers’
summary: The October Read With Jenna book club pick for October 2026 is Partita by Barbara Kingsolver.
story: Jenna Bush Hager picked a book by one of her “all-time favorite” authors for her October book club selection: “Partita” by Barbara Kingsolver.
“She’s on the Mt. Rushmore of writers for me,” Jenna says.
“Partita” is a followup to Kingsolver’s massive hit “Demon Copperhead,” which won the Pulitzer Prize in 2023.
It’s about a woman named Livia who looks back at her first romance when he unexpectedly contacts her decades after they met when she was studying piano in college.
“When a great love from her past comes back into her future, it has her ask the question, ‘How has my life ended up? Has it centered around the things I thought it would?” Jenna asks.
She says she loves the book because of how intimate it is. “It centers around what makes life beautiful,” she says.

The title, “Partita,” is a reference to a type of musical composition that is literally in parts. The theme is reflected in how the book weaves together the many parts of Livia’s life, as well as the events that shatter her life into those parts.
“We know within the first page Livia loses her brother, which sets her off on a journey to put the broken pieces of her together,” she says.
Jenna points to the epilogue of the book, which is a quote by Toni Morrison: “Sometimes you don’t survive whole. You just survive in part. But the grandeur in life is that attempt.”
